content.content:
1	---
2	title: "feat: xRegistry-backed message listing and typed subscription scaffolding"
3	type: feat
4	status: active
5	date: 2026-09-02
6	---
7	
8	# feat: xRegistry-backed message listing and typed subscription scaffolding
9	
10	**Home repo:** `intropy-cli` (this repository). The plan also touches two sibling
11	repos: `intropy-registry` (the xRegistry server, at `~/dev/intropy/intropy-registry`)
12	and the Intropy template library (fetched by `internal/template`). Paths below are
13	relative to the repo each unit names.
14	
15	## Overview
16	
17	Intropy now has a read-only, xRegistry-compliant registry of CloudEvents message
18	definitions, their payload JSON Schemas, and the endpoints that produce and
19	consume them. This plan makes the CLI a first-class consumer of that registry in
20	two steps:
21	
22	1. **Read:** new commands to list messages in the registry and show, for one
23	   message, exactly how to subscribe to it (CloudEvents type, schema reference,
24	   pubsub/topic channel, envelope mode).
25	2. **Scaffold:** a typed way for a template parameter to say "this component
26	   subscribes to message X from the registry", resolved at `int create` time
27	   into the concrete wiring values (`topic`, `pubsub`, `contract`, CloudEvents
28	   type) that template skeletons and `sys create` assembly already consume.
29	
30	The registry is read-only by design (`capabilities` advertises
31	`entities.mutable: false`); the CLI is a pure consumer. No registry writes are
32	in scope.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Problem Frame
37	
38	Today, wiring a new subscriber component is manual and unverified: a developer
39	must know the CloudEvents type, the Service Bus topic and Dapr pubsub component
40	name, and the C# contract type, and type them into template values by hand.
41	Nothing checks these against a source of truth, so drift between what a
42	component subscribes to and what producers actually publish is invisible until
43	runtime.
44	
45	The registry (`intropy-registry`) exists precisely to be that source of truth:
46	messagegroups/messages carry `envelopemetadata` (CloudEvents `type`, `source`),
47	`dataschemaxid` pointing at a versioned JSON Schema, and `protocol`; endpoints
48	carry `usage: [producer|subscriber]`, `channel: <pubsub>/<topic>`, and
49	`messagegroups` xid references. Everything a subscriber needs is already
50	resolvable over the conformant read-only API (`GET`, `?filter`, `?inline`,
51	`?doc`, `/export`).
52	
53	---
54	
55	## Requirements Trace
56	
57	- R1. A user can enumerate the messages in the registry from the CLI, in a
58	  table and as JSON.
59	- R2. A user can ask the CLI how to subscribe to one message and get a
60	  complete, correct answer: CloudEvents type, dataschema xid and format,
61	  pubsub component and topic, protocol and envelope mode.
62	- R3. A template can declare a parameter as a typed registry message
63	  reference; `int create` validates the reference against the registry and
64	  fails fast on unknown or malformed references.
65	- R4. At scaffold time the reference is resolved into the existing wiring
66	  values (`topic`, `pubsub`, plus a suggested `contract` and the CloudEvents
67	  type) so skeletons and `sys create` assembly work unchanged and offline.
68	- R5. The scaffold record (`.intropy/scaffold.json`) records both the resolved
69	  values and the message xid, so later commands can detect registry drift.
70	- R6. All new CLI surface follows the AGENTS.md writing and verb conventions
71	  (`list` enumerates, `show` prints one thing; stdout results, stderr status).
72	- R7. The registry remains spec-compliant; any registry-side change is
73	  optional, additive, and follows the xRegistry core/message/endpoint specs.
74	
75	---
76	
77	## Scope Boundaries
78	
79	- No mutation of the registry from the CLI — the registry is git-authored and
80	  read-only, and this plan does not change that.
81	- No contract code generation from JSON Schema (e.g. emitting C# records).
82	  The resolved `contract` value behaves exactly as it does today; generation
83	  is a deliberate follow-up.
84	- No changes to `sys create`/`sys update` assembly logic — the resolved wiring
85	  reuses the existing vocabulary verbatim.
86	- No drift-detection command (`int ... status` against the registry) in this
87	  plan; the recorded xid (R5) is the enabling groundwork only.
88	
89	### Deferred to Follow-Up Work
90	
91	- Contract codegen from `dataschemaxid` JSON Schema into a per-system
92	  `Contracts` project: separate plan; the largest open design space (naming,
93	  namespaces, generated-vs-handwritten boundaries).
94	- Registry-side ergonomics (per-messagegroup `channel`, or endpoint
95	  `?filter` over `messagegroups` xids): only if the client-side join in U2
96	  proves awkward at real registry sizes.
97	- A `diff`/`status`-style command comparing recorded xids against the live
98	  registry.
99	
100	---
101	
102	## Context & Research
103	
104	### Relevant Code and Patterns
105	
106	CLI (this repo):
107	
108	- `internal/registry/` — the **OCI** client for releases/templates. Name
109	  collision: the new client package must not be named `registry`. Use
110	  `internal/xregistry/`.
111	- `internal/template/wiring.go` — the wiring vocabulary (`KeyTopic`,
112	  `KeyContract`, `KeyPubsub`, `KeyAppID`) and the strict/lenient record
113	  readers (`RecordValue`, `SoftValue`). Resolved subscription values land
114	  here verbatim.
115	- `internal/template/manifest.go` — template manifest schema; `FieldSpec` is
116	  the prompter/CLI view of `spec.parameters.properties` and already carries
117	  prompt-only metadata (`Suggestions`) that never enters JSON Schema
118	  validation. The typed-reference annotation extends this seam.
119	- `internal/template/scaffold.go` — the scaffold record; additive fields do
120	  not require a `ScaffoldSchemaVersion` bump.
121	- `internal/template/scaffold_list.go`, `internal/system/blocks.go` — how
122	  recorded values feed workspace facts and system assembly
123	  (`parseTopicBlock` reads `topic`/`contract`/`pubsub`).
124	- `cmd/intropy/int_create.go`, `internal/template/create.go`,
125	  `internal/template/prepare.go`, `internal/template/prompt.go`,
126	  `internal/template/suggest.go` — the create pipeline: value resolution,
127	  prompting, suggestion sources, render.
128	- `internal/config/` — per-context config resolution (pattern for adding the
129	  registry base URL).
130	- `cmd/intropy/release_list.go`, `cmd/intropy/release_show.go` — command
131	  shape, output/JSON handling, and error style to mirror.
132	
133	Registry (`~/dev/intropy/intropy-registry`):
134	
135	- Read-only conformant API: `GET /messagegroups/{gid}/messages/{mid}`,
136	  `?filter` (all operators), `?inline` (nested paths, `*`), `?doc`, `/export`
137	  (byte-identical to `/?doc&inline=*,capabilities,modelsource`), `/model`,
138	  `/capabilities`. Write verbs return 405.
139	- Content negotiation (`src/http/negotiate.ts`): HTML wins only when
140	  `text/html` is specifically acceptable and beats wildcards. Go's
141	  `http.Client` sends no `Accept` header when unset (which the negotiator
142	  treats as JSON-safe), **but the CLI sends `Accept: application/json`
143	  explicitly** so intent is unambiguous and future portal routes cannot
144	  surprise it.
145	- Naming conventions (README): `messageid` is the full CloudEvents `type`;
146	  `channel` on endpoints is `<pubsub>/<topic>` — exactly the CLI's `pubsub`
147	  and `topic` wiring values joined by `/`.
148	- Message → channel join: endpoints reference messagegroups via xids;
149	  `usage: [producer]` + `messagegroups: [/messagegroups/<gid>]` identifies
150	  the producing endpoint, whose `channel` gives pubsub/topic.
151	
152	### Institutional Learnings
153	
154	- AGENTS.md (this repo) is the binding style contract for all new CLI
155	  surface: command verbs (`list`/`show` are the read-only verbs; new nouns
156	  hang under `int` like `sys`, `template`, `release`), flag description
157	  constants in `cmd/intropy/flagtext.go`, lowercase no-period status lines
158	  on stderr, front-loaded errors with remediation on a second line.
159	
160	### External References
161	
162	- xRegistry core spec and CloudEvents message/endpoint registry models —
163	  vendored copies live in `intropy-registry/spec/` (`core-model.schema.json`,
164	  `message-model.json`, `endpoint-model.json`) and are the authority for any
165	  registry-side change.
166	
167	---
168	
169	## Key Technical Decisions
170	
171	- **New noun `message`, not `registry`:** the CLI's "registry" already means
172	  the OCI release/template registry (`internal/registry`, `release`
173	  commands). Overloading it for xRegistry would be actively misleading.
174	  Commands: `int message list`, `int message show <messageid>`.
175	- **`/export` + client-side join, not N+1 queries:** the registry is small
176	  and git-backed; one `GET /export` yields messagegroups, messages, schemas,
177	  and endpoints in a single document, and `show` joins locally. This avoids
178	  encoding registry-size assumptions into the client and needs no
179	  registry-side changes. Revisit if the registry grows.
180	- **Typed reference is a manifest annotation, not a new value type in
181	  templates:** `spec.parameters.properties.<name>` gains an optional
182	  extension key (e.g. `x-intropy-message-ref: true`, or a `format` the CLI
183	  recognizes). Templates still render plain strings; the CLI resolves the
184	  reference into the existing wiring values before render. This keeps the
185	  template surface unchanged and makes resolution testable in the CLI alone.
186	- **Resolution happens once, at create time, and is recorded:** the scaffold
187	  record gains an additive field (e.g. `subscriptions: [{message: "<xid>",
188	  schemaVersion: "1"}]`) alongside the resolved `topic`/`pubsub`/`contract`
189	  values. Offline `sys create` and suggestions keep working from the resolved
190	  values; the xid enables future drift checks. No `ScaffoldSchemaVersion`
191	  bump (additive).
192	- **Channel ownership:** the producing endpoint's `channel`
193	  (`<pubsub>/<topic>`) is the source of truth for where to subscribe. If no
194	  producer endpoint exists for a messagegroup, `message show` reports the
195	  message fully and says the channel is not declared (a registry authoring
196	  gap, not a CLI error); scaffolding refuses the reference with a
197	  remediation line.
198	- **`contract` stays developer-owned, with a registry-derived suggestion:**
199	  the registry's `schemaid` (e.g. `product-export.v1`) is a kebab-case
200	  document id, not a C# type name, and no generated type exists until the
201	  deferred codegen follow-up. Deriving `contract` silently would record a
202	  type that exists nowhere. So the resolver *suggests* a contract name —
203	  strip the `.vN` suffix, kebab→Pascal (`product-export.v1` →
204	  `ProductExport`) — and the developer confirms or overrides it at the
205	  prompt (or via `--set contract=`). The schema xid and version recorded in
206	  `subscriptions` keep the provenance that a future codegen pass or drift
207	  check reconciles against. Collision handling for the suggestion (two
208	  schemaids mapping to one Pascal name) is a prompt-time concern only: the
209	  developer's confirmed value is what gets recorded.
210	- **Bare message ids must be unambiguous:** `message show <messageid>` and
211	  message-ref parameters accept a bare messageid; nothing in the registry
212	  prevents the same CloudEvents type in two messagegroups. A bare id that
213	  matches more than one message is an error listing the matching xids; the
214	  full xid form always resolves exactly.
215	- **Recorded schema version comes from the schema resource's default
216	  version:** `dataschemaxid` points at the schema resource (no
217	  `/versions/<id>` suffix), so the resolver reads the schema's default
218	  version id from the export document and records that in `subscriptions`.
219	
220	---
221	
222	## Open Questions
223	
224	### Resolved During Planning
225	
226	- Does the registry API suffice as-is? Yes — `/export`, `?doc`, and the
227	  endpoint `channel` convention cover list, show, and resolution without
228	  registry changes.
229	- Where does the registry base URL live? Resolved through the existing
230	  `config.Resolve` precedence — `--registry-url` flag > `INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL`
231	  env var > customer context in the config file — matching every sibling
232	  setting (`INTROPY_GITOPS_REPO`, `INTROPY_TEMPLATE_REPO`). New shared flag
233	  constant in `cmd/intropy/flagtext.go`. The config key must exist before
234	  users can set it: `config.Load` uses `KnownFields(true)`, so an unknown
235	  key in the config file is a load error.
236	- How is `contract` derived from the registry? It isn't — it stays
237	  developer-owned with a registry-derived suggestion (see Key Technical
238	  Decisions). Silent derivation would record a C# type that exists nowhere
239	  until the codegen follow-up.
240	- Must the CLI handle registry unavailability during `int create`? Yes:
241	  non-registry templates are unaffected; a template *with* a message-ref
242	  parameter fails fast with a front-loaded error naming the registry and the
243	  unreachable URL.
244	
245	### Deferred to Implementation
246	
247	- Exact extension-key name and shape in the template manifest
248	  (`x-intropy-message-ref` boolean vs. a structured object): settle against
249	  the real template library during U4.
250	- Whether `message show` renders the schema document inline (via `?doc`) or
251	  only its xid/version: decide against actual output readability.
252	- How multiple producer endpoints for one messagegroup are surfaced (list
253	  all channels vs. error): depends on whether the registry ever has more
254	  than one.
255	
256	---
257	
258	## High-Level Technical Design
259	
260	> *This illustrates the intended approach and is directional guidance for
261	> review, not implementation specification. The implementing agent should
262	> treat it as context, not code to reproduce.*
263	
264	```mermaid
265	flowchart LR
266	    subgraph CLI
267	      MC[int message list/show] --> XR[internal/xregistry client]
268	      CR[int create] --> RES[message-ref resolver]
269	      RES --> XR
270	      RES --> SC[.intropy/scaffold.json\nvalues + subscriptions]
271	    end
272	    XR -->|GET /export, /messagegroups/... Accept: application/json| REG[(intropy-registry\nread-only xRegistry API)]
273	    SC --> SYS[sys create assembly\nexisting wiring vocabulary]
274	    SC --> SKEL[template skeletons\nplain string values]
275	```
276	
277	Resolution data flow (create time, per message-ref parameter):
278	
279	1. Prompt/flag yields a message reference (`<messageid>` or full xid
280	   `/messagegroups/<gid>/messages/<mid>`).
281	2. Resolver fetches `/export` (cached per create run) and locates the
282	   message; unknown id → usage error listing close matches.
283	3. Resolver finds the producer endpoint for the message's group and splits
284	   `channel` into `pubsub` + `topic`.
285	4. Resolver derives the CloudEvents `type` from `envelopemetadata`, reads
286	   the schema resource at `dataschemaxid` for its id and default version,
287	   and builds the suggested `contract` name (strip `.vN`, kebab→Pascal).
288	5. Values map gains `topic` and `pubsub`, the `contract` suggestion feeds
289	   the prompt (developer confirms or overrides), and the recorded
290	   `subscriptions` entry carries the message xid, schemaid and versionid;
291	   render proceeds exactly as today.
292	
293	---
294	
295	## Implementation Units
296	
297	- [x] U1. **xRegistry client package (`internal/xregistry`)**
298	
299	**Goal:** A typed, testable read-only client for the registry — fetch the
300	export document and individual entities, with models for messagegroups,
301	messages, schemas, and endpoints — plus the config plumbing that gives it a
302	base URL.
303	
304	**Requirements:** R1, R2, R7
305	
306	**Dependencies:** None
307	
308	**Files:**
309	- Create: `internal/xregistry/client.go`
310	- Create: `internal/xregistry/types.go`
311	- Modify: `internal/config/` (registry URL in the resolved config,
312	  following the flag > env > context > file precedence; the config key
313	  must be a known field before users can set it)
314	- Test: `internal/xregistry/client_test.go`
315	
316	**Approach:**
317	- One constructor taking base URL + `http.Client`; every request sends
318	  `Accept: application/json` (explicit intent; the negotiator also treats
319	  an absent or wildcard-only Accept as JSON, but the explicit header is
320	  the contract).

476	  not `create.go`: the dashboard's form flow goes through `PrepareCreate`

---
title: "feat: xRegistry-backed message listing and typed subscription scaffolding"
type: feat
status: active
date: 2026-09-02
---

# feat: xRegistry-backed message listing and typed subscription scaffolding

**Home repo:** `intropy-cli` (this repository). The plan also touches two sibling
repos: `intropy-registry` (the xRegistry server, at `~/dev/intropy/intropy-registry`)
and the Intropy template library (fetched by `internal/template`). Paths below are
relative to the repo each unit names.

## Overview

Intropy now has a read-only, xRegistry-compliant registry of CloudEvents message
definitions, their payload JSON Schemas, and the endpoints that produce and
consume them. This plan makes the CLI a first-class consumer of that registry in
two steps:

1. **Read:** new commands to list messages in the registry and show, for one
   message, exactly how to subscribe to it (CloudEvents type, schema reference,
   pubsub/topic channel, envelope mode).
2. **Scaffold:** a typed way for a template parameter to say "this component
   subscribes to message X from the registry", resolved at `int create` time
   into the concrete wiring values (`topic`, `pubsub`, `contract`, CloudEvents
   type) that template skeletons and `sys create` assembly already consume.

The registry is read-only by design (`capabilities` advertises
`entities.mutable: false`); the CLI is a pure consumer. No registry writes are
in scope.

---

## Problem Frame

Today, wiring a new subscriber component is manual and unverified: a developer
must know the CloudEvents type, the Service Bus topic and Dapr pubsub component
name, and the C# contract type, and type them into template values by hand.
Nothing checks these against a source of truth, so drift between what a
component subscribes to and what producers actually publish is invisible until
runtime.

The registry (`intropy-registry`) exists precisely to be that source of truth:
messagegroups/messages carry `envelopemetadata` (CloudEvents `type`, `source`),
`dataschemaxid` pointing at a versioned JSON Schema, and `protocol`; endpoints
carry `usage: [producer|subscriber]`, `channel: <pubsub>/<topic>`, and
`messagegroups` xid references. Everything a subscriber needs is already
resolvable over the conformant read-only API (`GET`, `?filter`, `?inline`,
`?doc`, `/export`).

---

## Requirements Trace

- R1. A user can enumerate the messages in the registry from the CLI, in a
  table and as JSON.
- R2. A user can ask the CLI how to subscribe to one message and get a
  complete, correct answer: CloudEvents type, dataschema xid and format,
  pubsub component and topic, protocol and envelope mode.
- R3. A template can declare a parameter as a typed registry message
  reference; `int create` validates the reference against the registry and
  fails fast on unknown or malformed references.
- R4. At scaffold time the reference is resolved into the existing wiring
  values (`topic`, `pubsub`, plus a suggested `contract` and the CloudEvents
  type) so skeletons and `sys create` assembly work unchanged and offline.
- R5. The scaffold record (`.intropy/scaffold.json`) records both the resolved
  values and the message xid, so later commands can detect registry drift.
- R6. All new CLI surface follows the AGENTS.md writing and verb conventions
  (`list` enumerates, `show` prints one thing; stdout results, stderr status).
- R7. The registry remains spec-compliant; any registry-side change is
  optional, additive, and follows the xRegistry core/message/endpoint specs.

---

## Scope Boundaries

- No mutation of the registry from the CLI — the registry is git-authored and
  read-only, and this plan does not change that.
- No contract code generation from JSON Schema (e.g. emitting C# records).
  The resolved `contract` value behaves exactly as it does today; generation
  is a deliberate follow-up.
- No changes to `sys create`/`sys update` assembly logic — the resolved wiring
  reuses the existing vocabulary verbatim.
- No drift-detection command (`int ... status` against the registry) in this
  plan; the recorded xid (R5) is the enabling groundwork only.

### Deferred to Follow-Up Work

- Contract codegen from `dataschemaxid` JSON Schema into a per-system
  `Contracts` project: separate plan; the largest open design space (naming,
  namespaces, generated-vs-handwritten boundaries).
- Registry-side ergonomics (per-messagegroup `channel`, or endpoint
  `?filter` over `messagegroups` xids): only if the client-side join in U2
  proves awkward at real registry sizes.
- A `diff`/`status`-style command comparing recorded xids against the live
  registry.

Registry (`~/dev/intropy/intropy-registry`):

- Read-only conformant API: `GET /messagegroups/{gid}/messages/{mid}`,

  (byte-identical to `/?doc&inline=*,capabilities,modelsource`), `/model`,
  `/capabilities`. Write verbs return 405.
- Content negotiation (`src/http/negotiate.ts`): HTML wins only when
  `text/html` is specifically acceptable and beats wildcards. Go's
  `http.Client` sends no `Accept` header when unset (which the negotiator
  treats as JSON-safe), **but the CLI sends `Accept: application/json`

  surprise it.

  `channel` on endpoints is `<pubsub>/<topic>` — exactly the CLI's `pubsub`
  and `topic` wiring values joined by `/`.
- Message → channel join: endpoints reference messagegroups via xids;
  `usage: [producer]` + `messagegroups: [/messagegroups/<gid>]` identifies
  the producing endpoint, whose `channel` gives pubsub/topic.

## Key Technical Decisions

- **New noun `message`, not `registry`:** the CLI's "registry" already means
  the OCI release/template registry (`internal/registry`, `release`
  commands). Overloading it for xRegistry would be actively misleading.
  Commands: `int message list`, `int message show <messageid>`.
- **`/export` + client-side join, not N+1 queries:** the registry is small
  and git-backed; one `GET /export` yields messagegroups, messages, schemas,
  and endpoints in a single document, and `show` joins locally. This avoids
  encoding registry-size assumptions into the client and needs no
  registry-side changes. Revisit if the registry grows.
- **Typed reference is a manifest annotation, not a new value type in
  templates:** `spec.parameters.properties.<name>` gains an optional
  extension key (e.g. `x-intropy-message-ref: true`, or a `format` the CLI
  recognizes). Templates still render plain strings; the CLI resolves the
  reference into the existing wiring values before render. This keeps the
  template surface unchanged and makes resolution testable in the CLI alone.
- **Resolution happens once, at create time, and is recorded:** the scaffold
  record gains an additive field (e.g. `subscriptions: [{message: "<xid>",
  schemaVersion: "1"}]`) alongside the resolved `topic`/`pubsub`/`contract`
  values. Offline `sys create` and suggestions keep working from the resolved
  values; the xid enables future drift checks. No `ScaffoldSchemaVersion`
  bump (additive).
- **Channel ownership:** the producing endpoint's `channel`
  (`<pubsub>/<topic>`) is the source of truth for where to subscribe. If no
  producer endpoint exists for a messagegroup, `message show` reports the
  message fully and says the channel is not declared (a registry authoring
  gap, not a CLI error); scaffolding refuses the reference with a
  remediation line.
- **`contract` stays developer-owned, with a registry-derived suggestion:**
  the registry's `schemaid` (e.g. `product-export.v1`) is a kebab-case
  document id, not a C# type name, and no generated type exists until the
  deferred codegen follow-up. Deriving `contract` silently would record a
  type that exists nowhere. So the resolver *suggests* a contract name —
  strip the `.vN` suffix, kebab→Pascal (`product-export.v1` →
  `ProductExport`) — and the developer confirms or overrides it at the
  prompt (or via `--set contract=`). The schema xid and version recorded in
  `subscriptions` keep the provenance that a future codegen pass or drift
  check reconciles against. Collision handling for the suggestion (two
  schemaids mapping to one Pascal name) is a prompt-time concern only: the
  developer's confirmed value is what gets recorded.
- **Bare message ids must be unambiguous:** `message show <messageid>` and
  message-ref parameters accept a bare messageid; nothing in the registry
  prevents the same CloudEvents type in two messagegroups. A bare id that
  matches more than one message is an error listing the matching xids; the
  full xid form always resolves exactly.
- **Recorded schema version comes from the schema resource's default
  version:** `dataschemaxid` points at the schema resource (no
  `/versions/<id>` suffix), so the resolver reads the schema's default
  version id from the export document and records that in `subscriptions`.

## Open Questions

### Resolved During Planning

- Does the registry API suffice as-is? Yes — `/export`, `?doc`, and the
  endpoint `channel` convention cover list, show, and resolution without
  registry changes.
- Where does the registry base URL live? Resolved through the existing
  `config.Resolve` precedence — `--registry-url` flag > `INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL`
  env var > customer context in the config file — matching every sibling
  setting (`INTROPY_GITOPS_REPO`, `INTROPY_TEMPLATE_REPO`). New shared flag
  constant in `cmd/intropy/flagtext.go`. The config key must exist before
  users can set it: `config.Load` uses `KnownFields(true)`, so an unknown
  key in the config file is a load error.
- How is `contract` derived from the registry? It isn't — it stays
  developer-owned with a registry-derived suggestion (see Key Technical
  Decisions). Silent derivation would record a C# type that exists nowhere
  until the codegen follow-up.
- Must the CLI handle registry unavailability during `int create`? Yes:
  non-registry templates are unaffected; a template *with* a message-ref
  parameter fails fast with a front-loaded error naming the registry and the
  unreachable URL.

### Deferred to Implementation

- Exact extension-key name and shape in the template manifest
  (`x-intropy-message-ref` boolean vs. a structured object): settle against
  the real template library during U4.
- Whether `message show` renders the schema document inline (via `?doc`) or
  only its xid/version: decide against actual output readability.
- How multiple producer endpoints for one messagegroup are surfaced (list
  all channels vs. error): depends on whether the registry ever has more
  than one.

## High-Level Technical Design

> *This illustrates the intended approach and is directional guidance for
> review, not implementation specification. The implementing agent should
> treat it as context, not code to reproduce.*

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph CLI
      MC[int message list/show] --> XR[internal/xregistry client]
      CR[int create] --> RES[message-ref resolver]
      RES --> XR
      RES --> SC[.intropy/scaffold.json\nvalues + subscriptions]
    end
    XR -->|GET /export, /messagegroups/... Accept: application/json| REG[(intropy-registry\nread-only xRegistry API)]
    SC --> SYS[sys create assembly\nexisting wiring vocabulary]
    SC --> SKEL[template skeletons\nplain string values]
```

Resolution data flow (create time, per message-ref parameter):

1. Prompt/flag yields a message reference (`<messageid>` or full xid
   `/messagegroups/<gid>/messages/<mid>`).
2. Resolver fetches `/export` (cached per create run) and locates the
   message; unknown id → usage error listing close matches.
3. Resolver finds the producer endpoint for the message's group and splits
   `channel` into `pubsub` + `topic`.
4. Resolver derives the CloudEvents `type` from `envelopemetadata`, reads
   the schema resource at `dataschemaxid` for its id and default version,
   and builds the suggested `contract` name (strip `.vN`, kebab→Pascal).
5. Values map gains `topic` and `pubsub`, the `contract` suggestion feeds
   the prompt (developer confirms or overrides), and the recorded
   `subscriptions` entry carries the message xid, schemaid and versionid;
   render proceeds exactly as today.

## System-Wide Impact

- **Interaction graph:** new noun `message` under `int`; one new package
  `internal/xregistry`; one new resolver hook in the create pipeline. No
  existing command changes behavior.
- **Error propagation:** registry errors surface as front-loaded command
  errors; inside `create`, resolution failures abort before any file
  writes (no partial scaffolds).
- **State lifecycle risks:** the scaffold record is the only persisted
  state; additive field, old CLIs ignore it, new CLIs tolerate its absence.
- **API surface parity:** the dashboard (`internal/dashboard`) renders
  template forms from `FieldSpec`; a new `FieldSpec` field is additive JSON
  but the dashboard will not offer registry-backed suggestions until a
  follow-up — note this in the dashboard docs if it renders the new field.
- **Integration coverage:** U4's fixture-registry create test and U5's
  end-to-end render are the two places mocks alone would not prove the
  wiring.
- **Unchanged invariants:** `internal/registry` (OCI) is untouched; `sys
  create`/`update` assembly logic is untouched; the manifest JSON Schema
  contract for values is untouched; the registry stays read-only.

## Risks & Dependencies

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| "Registry" name confusion (OCI vs xRegistry) in code and UX | New package `internal/xregistry`, new noun `message`; no reuse of "registry" in user-facing strings without qualification |
| Registry not yet deployed at a stable URL (`baseurl: https://registry.intropy.io` is aspirational) | URL is config, not constant; all tests use fixture servers; feature works against `task dev` locally from day one |
| Registry model drifts from the CLI's typed models | Models are built from `/export`, which the registry guarantees byte-identical to the inlined root; a smoke check against the real server is part of U1 verification |
| Producer endpoint missing or ambiguous for a group | Explicit "no producer declared" path in U2; refusal-with-remediation in U4; registry authoring convention documented |
| Annotated templates meeting old CLIs | Extension key is inert to older versions; template and CLI releases are independent |

## Implementation Notes

Recorded at execution time (2026-09-02); where these differ from the unit
text above, the notes are what shipped.

- **Registry fetch is lazy in effect, not just in scope.** The original
  design fetched the export up front whenever a template declared a
  message-ref parameter and failed the create on any fetch error.
  End-to-end verification with the real loader template showed this broke
  the manual topic/contract flow whenever the registry was down or
  unconfigured. As shipped: the fetch feeds only prompt suggestions, a
  fetch failure degrades to a stderr warning, and a hard error requires an
  actual message-ref value (commit `fix(template): require the registry
  only when a message reference is used`).
- **Injection conflict rule refined.** The plan said "a conflicting
  explicit value is an error". As shipped, only a conflicting `--set`
  errors; template defaults, `spec.values` derivations and values-file
  values yield to the registry with a stderr note. Motivation: the loader
  derives `pubsub: 'pubsub'` as a platform convention, and conventions
  must not conflict with the registry's fact about a specific message
  (commit `fix(template): let registry override derived wiring values`).
- **Contract suggestion timing.** The plan sketched the suggestion feeding
  the contract prompt. As shipped, the suggestion fills an unset contract
  post-resolution with a stderr note (same visibility regime as facts
  prefill); a contract the developer supplied always stands. Prompt-time
  suggestion would require registry access inside the prompt loop and is a
  possible follow-up.
- **Message name/description live on the default version** in real export
  documents (the server normalizes message-level attributes onto the
  version); `ResolvedMessage.DisplayName/DisplayDescription` hide the
  split. Found by live smoke against `task dev` in intropy-registry.
- **Live verification** (U1/U2/U5): `int message list`, `int message show`
  (plain and JSON, error paths) run against the real registry; the edited
  loader manifest was driven end-to-end through `Create` against the live
  registry (subscription flow resolves; legacy flow untouched; anyOf guard
  validates) via a throwaway test, since the library's `intropy.io/v1`
  apiVersion rename is ahead of this branch — the CLI-side rename rides
  the existing `chore/intropy-dev-to-io` branch.
- **U5 landed in intropy-templates** on branch `feat/loader-message-ref`
  (not pushed): the loader gains an optional `subscription` parameter,

=== README ===
# intropy-registry

A narrow, [xRegistry](https://xregistry.io)-compliant registry for CloudEvents
definitions, their payload schemas, and the endpoints that produce and consume
them.

Standards-compliant, deliberately small. It borrows EventCatalog's git-as-source-of-truth
authoring model and its look, but not its surface area — there are no domains,
flows, ADRs, teams, ownership, changelog, AI agents or generators.

## Why

Intropy has no contract governance. Message contracts are plain C# `record` types
in a per-System `Contracts` project, shared by `ProjectReference`, so cross-team
and cross-repo contract evolution is unguarded. No JSON Schema, Avro or Protobuf
exists for any business payload, and the CloudEvents `dataschema` attribute is
never set and never read.

This gives you a resolvable `dataschema` URI, a reviewable diff when a contract
changes, and one readable page per event.

## Shape

Git-first and **read-only**. Definitions are authored as files under `registry/`
and reviewed in a PR; the server exposes them over a conformant read-only
xRegistry API. The core spec explicitly provides for this — `/capabilities`
advertises `available.entities.mutable: false`, and every write verb returns 405.

Three group types, from the CloudEvents Registry:

| Group | Resource | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `messagegroups` | `messages` | `hasdocument: false`, `maxversions: 1` — pure metadata |
| `schemagroups` | `schemas` | documents, versions, format and compatibility validation |
| `endpoints` | *(imports `messages`)* | producers and consumers, referencing messagegroups |

Narrowed to `CloudEvents/1.0` envelopes, `JsonSchema/draft/2020-12` payloads and
the `AMQP/1.0` and `HTTP` protocols Intropy actually deploys. The narrowing is one
object — `NARROWING` in `src/registry/model.ts` — and widening it is an edit there
and nowhere else.

## Authoring

```
registry/
  registry.yaml                                  registryid, name, baseurl
  messagegroups/<messagegroupid>.yaml            the group and its messages
  schemagroups/<schemagroupid>/
    group.yaml
    <schemaid>/
      schema.yaml                                format, compatibility, default version
      1.json                                     version documents, named by versionid
  endpoints/<endpointid>.yaml
```

`createdat` / `modifiedat` fall back to file mtime, and `epoch` defaults to 1.
Set them explicitly for reproducible builds — a git-backed registry has no natural
epoch counter.

### Naming

| id | Rule | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `messagegroupid` | `<reverse-domain>.<customer>.<domain>` | `io.intropy.maxbo.product` |
| `messageid` | the full CloudEvents `type` | `io.intropy.maxbo.product.export` |
| `schemagroupid` | mirrors `messagegroupid` | `io.intropy.maxbo.product` |
| `schemaid` | `<contract-kebab>.v<major>` | `product-export.v1` |
| `endpointid` | Dapr app-id / component name (DNS-1123 label) | `perfion-extractor` |
| `channel` | `<pubsub>/<topic>` | `product-distribution-pubsub/sbt-test-product-extractor-001` |

A breaking change means a **new schema resource**, not a new version — hence the
major version in `schemaid`. That is why versions can be validated for
compatibility at all.

Non-conforming event types are a **warning**, never an error. The extractor
template currently generates a non-reverse-DNS form, so rejecting would make the
registry unable to hold events that already exist in production. More broadly:
an invalid entity is dropped with an error, an unresolved reference is kept with
a warning. A registry mid-edit is still worth serving.

## Running

[go-task](https://taskfile.dev) is the front door; the npm scripts underneath still work.

```
task                # list everything
task dev            # the real thing on :8787 — API, portal and negotiation
task dev:site       # astro on :4321 with HMR — fast UI work, no negotiation or API
task verify         # the full gate: typecheck, tests, build, live conformance
```

Driving it from an agent or a script:

```
task dev:bg         # start in the background, wait until it answers
task dev:status
task dev:logs
task dev:stop
```

`task verify` starts a server, runs the 54 spec assertions against it, and stops
it again — including when the assertions fail, so a red run never leaves a stray
process holding the port.

The Worker rehydrates the built tree at cold start and serializes per request,
so a plain GET and a `?filter`'d GET come from the same code path and cannot drift.

## Portal and API on one URL

xRegistry puts the registry root at `/`, and a portal wants a page there too. One
path can only be one thing, so the two share every path and are separated by
`Accept`:

```bash
curl        localhost:8787/                      # JSON — the registry root
curl -H 'Accept: text/html' localhost:8787/      # HTML — the portal
open        http://localhost:8787/               # HTML
```

The rule (`src/http/negotiate.ts`) is that HTML wins only when `text/html` is
acceptable *specifically* and at least as strongly as `application/json`, and more
strongly than any wildcard. A wildcard alone is never enough — **curl sends `*/*`
and must keep getting JSON**. Every response carries `Vary: Accept` so a cache
cannot serve one to the other.

Two deliberate exceptions:

- `/model`, `/capabilities` and `/export` are API-only. They have no page, so a
  browser gets JSON.
- An API path with no portal page yet **falls back to JSON** rather than 404ing.
  The resource does exist; only the page is missing. Phase 2 fills these in.

`run_worker_first = true` in `wrangler.toml` is load-bearing. Without it
Cloudflare's asset router serves `dist/site/index.html` for `/` before the Worker
ever runs, and every API client gets the portal instead of the registry root.
Unit tests cannot catch this — they call the Worker directly — so it is asserted
in `scripts/conformance.sh` against a real server.

## Compliance

Implemented: `GET` on every entity path, `/model`, `/capabilities`, `/export`,
`?filter` (all operators, AND within a parameter, OR across parameters), `?inline`
(nested paths, `*`, relative to the entity retrieved), `?doc` / `?nodoc`,
`Link: rel=xregistry-root`, and 405 on every write.

`GET /export` is byte-identical to `GET /?doc&inline=*,capabilities,modelsource`,
which is asserted in both the test suite and the conformance script.

Not implemented, and not advertised: mutation, pagination, auth.

`formatvalidated` is earned, not asserted — every schema document is compiled with
ajv at build time and the flag is set from the result.

### Two upstream notes

**The published meta-schema rejects the published schema model.**
`spec/schema/model.json` uses `validateformat`, `validatecompatibility` and
`strictvalidation`, all documented in `core/model.md`, but
`core/model.schema.json` forbids them via `additionalProperties: false`. We keep
the keys — `validateformat: true` is what makes `formatvalidated` mean anything —
and `tests/model.test.ts` asserts our flattening adds no violations beyond those
three. If upstream fixes the meta-schema, the allowlist empties and the test
tightens on its own.

**The vendored meta-schema declares `https://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#`**,
while ajv registers draft-07 under `http://`. The test registers the alias.

## Status

Phases 1 and 2 are complete: the read-only API, content negotiation, and the
portal — overview, events catalog with filtering, event pages, schema pages with
version diffs, and endpoint pages, on the Manual light surface.

Portal routes mirror the xRegistry paths, so `/messagegroups/<g>/messages/<m>` is
both the API resource and the page. `/events` is the one portal-only route: a flat
catalog the API has no equivalent for.

All four phases are complete: the read-only API, content negotiation, the portal,
the topology graph, a `⌘K` command palette, and the accessibility and caching
pass. Lighthouse is 100 for accessibility, best practices and SEO on every page
type.

Portal-only routes: `/events`, `/graph`, `/api`. Everything else mirrors an
xRegistry path.

ever runs, and every API client gets the portal instead of the registry root.
Unit tests cannot catch this — they call the Worker directly — so it is asserted
in `scripts/conformance.sh` against a real server.

## Compliance

Implemented: `GET` on every entity path, `/model`, `/capabilities`, `/export`,
`?filter` (all operators, AND within a parameter, OR across parameters), `?inline`
(nested paths, `*`, relative to the entity retrieved), `?doc` / `?nodoc`,
`Link: rel=xregistry-root`, and 405 on every write.

`GET /export` is byte-identical to `GET /?doc&inline=*,capabilities,modelsource`,
which is asserted in both the test suite and the conformance script.

Not implemented, and not advertised: mutation, pagination, auth.

`formatvalidated` is earned, not asserted — every schema document is compiled with
ajv at build time and the flag is set from the result.

### Two upstream notes

**The published meta-schema rejects the published schema model.**
`spec/schema/model.json` uses `validateformat`, `validatecompatibility` and
`strictvalidation`, all documented in `core/model.md`, but
`core/model.schema.json` forbids them via `additionalProperties: false`. We keep
the keys — `validateformat: true` is what makes `formatvalidated` mean anything —
and `tests/model.test.ts` asserts our flattening adds no violations beyond those
three. If upstream fixes the meta-schema, the allowlist empties and the test
tightens on its own.

**The vendored meta-schema declares `https://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#`**,
while ajv registers draft-07 under `http://`. The test registers the alias.

## Status

Phases 1 and 2 are complete: the read-only API, content negotiation, and the
portal — overview, events catalog with filtering, event pages, schema pages with
version diffs, and endpoint pages, on the Manual light surface.

Portal routes mirror the xRegistry paths, so `/messagegroups/<g>/messages/<m>` is
both the API resource and the page. `/events` is the one portal-only route: a flat
catalog the API has no equivalent for.

All four phases are complete: the read-only API, content negotiation, the portal,
the topology graph, a `⌘K` command palette, and the accessibility and caching
pass. Lighthouse is 100 for accessibility, best practices and SEO on every page
type.

Portal-only routes: `/events`, `/graph`, `/api`. Everything else mirrors an
xRegistry path.

=== messagegroup product ===
messagegroupid: io.intropy.maxbo.product
name: Maxbo product distribution
description: >-
  Events emitted by the Maxbo product-distribution system. The Perfion extractor
  runs as a batch job, writes one JSONL blob per entity type to blob storage, and
  publishes a single event referencing those blobs — records are not carried inline.
envelope: CloudEvents/1.0
protocol: AMQP/1.0

messages:
  io.intropy.maxbo.product.export:
    name: Product export completed
    description: >-
      Emitted once per batch, after all entity JSONL blobs have been written to the
      export container and before the consumed inputs are archived.
    envelope: CloudEvents/1.0
    envelopemetadata:
      specversion:
        value: '1.0'
        type: string
      type:
        value: io.intropy.maxbo.product.export
        type: string
        required: true
      source:
        value: urn:maxbo:perfion
        type: uri
        required: true
        description: The originating extractor. Loaders use it for echo prevention.
      subject:
        type: string
        required: true
        description: The export id; equal to the event id.
      id:
        type: string
        required: true
        description: The export id. Feeds the Idempotency Service.
      time:
        type: timestamp
        required: true
      datacontenttype:
        value: application/json
        type: string
    protocol: AMQP/1.0
    dataschemaformat: JsonSchema/draft/2020-12
    dataschemaxid: /schemagroups/io.intropy.maxbo.product/schemas/product-export.v1
    datacontenttype: application/json
=== endpoint kat-product-loader ===
endpointid: kat-product-loader
name: KAT product service loader
description: >-
  Subscribes to the product export event and loads the referenced JSONL blobs
  into the KAT product service. Dapr delivers via HTTP push to the route
  registered by MapSubscribeHandler.
usage:
  - subscriber
channel: product-distribution-pubsub/sbt-test-product-extractor-001
envelope: CloudEvents/1.0
envelopeoptions:
  mode: structured
  format: application/cloudevents+json
protocol: HTTP
protocoloptions:
  method: POST
  deployed: true
  endpoints:
    - uri: /events/sbt-test-product-extractor-001
messagegroups:
  - /messagegroups/io.intropy.maxbo.product
=== endpoint perfion-extractor ===
endpointid: perfion-extractor
name: Perfion product extractor
description: >-
  Batch extractor for the Perfion PIM. Runs to completion as a CronJob, writes
  JSONL blobs, then publishes one export event. Envelope is built across
  CloudEventSerializeStep (id, subject, time, datacontenttype, data) and
  DaprTopicPublisher (source, type).
usage:
  - producer
channel: product-distribution-pubsub/sbt-test-product-extractor-001
envelope: CloudEvents/1.0
envelopeoptions:
  mode: structured
  format: application/cloudevents+json
protocol: AMQP/1.0
protocoloptions:
  deployed: true
  endpoints:
    - uri: amqp://product-distribution-pubsub/sbt-test-product-extractor-001
messagegroups:
  - /messagegroups/io.intropy.maxbo.product
=== schema.yaml ===
name: Product export payload
description: >-
  Body of the export CloudEvent (the `data` member). Property names follow the
  System.Text.Json camelCase policy — first character lowercased only, so
  GTIN becomes gTIN — and nulls are omitted.
format: JsonSchema/draft/2020-12
compatibility: backward
=== schema doc 2.json ===
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://registry.intropy.io/schemagroups/io.intropy.maxbo.product/schemas/product-export.v1/versions/2",
  "title": "Export Event",
  "description": "Body of the export CloudEvent (the `data` member).",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "exportId",
    "container",
    "files"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "exportId": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Unique id of the batch run; also the CloudEvent id and subject."
    },
    "container": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Blob storage container holding the referenced JSONL blobs."
    },
    "files": {
      "type": "array",
      "description": "One entry per entity type written in this batch.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/ExportEventFile"
      }
    },
    "startedAt": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date-time",
      "description": "When the batch run started. Added in version 2; optional, so version 1 producers remain valid."
    }
  },
  "$defs": {
    "ExportEventFile": {
      "title": "Export Event File",
      "description": "Pointer to a single JSONL blob produced for one entity type.",
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": [
        "entityType",
        "blob",
        "recordCount",
        "rejectCount"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "entityType": {
          "type": "string",
          "description": "Logical entity type carried by this blob.",
          "enum": [
            "product",
            "category",
            "gtin",
            "image",
            "document",
            "product-attribute",
            "unit-conversion"
          ]
        },
        "blob": {
          "type": "string",
          "description": "Blob name (path within `container`) of the JSONL file. Each line is one record of the entity type's target schema."
        },
        "recordCount": {
          "type": "integer",
          "description": "Number of valid records written to the blob."
        },
        "rejectCount": {
          "type": "integer",
          "description": "Number of source items rejected during validation."
        },
        "bytes": {
          "type": "integer",
          "description": "Size of the blob in bytes. Added in version 2."
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

apiVersion: intropy.io/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: loader
  title: Loader Integration
  description: Long-running ASP.NET loader that subscribes to a Dapr pub/sub topic over HTTP delivery, runs each delivered message through the Intropy loader pipeline, and writes the result through a local destination folder binding.
  tags:
    - example
    - dotnet
    - dapr
    - loader
  labels:
    intropy.io/template-level: example
    intropy.io/block-kind: loader
    intropy.io/data-flow: "out"

spec:
  parameters:
    type: object
    required:
      - name
      - organization
    # The wiring comes from one of two sources: a message registry
    # reference (subscription), which the CLI expands into topic, pubsub
    # and a contract suggestion, or the topic and contract typed by hand.
    # The registry path is the primary one: topic and contract are marked
    # derived so prompts and forms leave them to the expansion, and the
    # manual path is an explicit opt-out (--set on the CLI, a toggle in
    # the dashboard) rather than an equal choice.
    anyOf:
      - required: [subscription]
      - required: [topic, contract]
    properties:
      name:
        type: string
        title: Project name
        description: PascalCase identifier used for the .NET project, root namespace, and assembly. Dot-separated segments are allowed for nested namespaces (e.g. OrderLoader or Int1055.OrderLoader).
        pattern: "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*(\\.[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)*$"
      organization:
        type: string
        title: Organization
        description: PascalCase name of the organization the integration runs for. Becomes the telemetry ServiceNamespace and the business-incident source URN (urn:<organization>:<component>).
        pattern: "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$"
      subscription:
        type: string
        title: Message subscription
        description: Message to subscribe to, as a message id or xid from the Intropy message registry (int message list). When set, the CLI resolves the topic, pubsub component and a contract suggestion from the registry; leave empty to wire topic and contract by hand.
        x-intropy-message-ref: true
      topic:
        type: string
        title: Topic
        description: The pub/sub topic the loader subscribes to. This is the loader's half of the system contract — scaffold the publishing extractor with the same value. Filled from the registry when subscription is set; only set it by hand when subscribing to a topic the registry does not declare.
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
        x-intropy-derived: true
      contract:
        type: string
        title: Contract type
        description: PascalCase name of the shared-contracts record the topic carries — the other half of the system contract, recorded in .intropy/scaffold.json for `intropy sys create` to type the topic with. The sample logic uses Order. Suggested from the message's schema when subscription is set.
        pattern: "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$"
        x-intropy-derived: true
      idempotencyAppId:
        type: string
        title: Idempotency service app-id
        description: Dapr app-id of the Idempotency Service. The default matches the platform-services deployment.
        default: "idempotency-service.services"
      businessIncidentsAppId:
        type: string
        title: Business incident service app-id
        description: Dapr app-id of the Business Incident Service. The default matches the platform-services deployment.
        default: "business-incident-service.services"
      empty:
        type: boolean
        title: Empty bodies
        description: When true, strip sample business logic from pipeline step bodies. The resulting project compiles and starts under Dapr, but every step throws NotImplementedException so a migration agent can fill them in. The idempotency and business-incident wiring stays (the loader pipeline requires it); idempotency keys off CloudEvent Subject/Time from the context, so there are no extractor lambdas to stub.
        default: true
  values:
    appId: '{{ .name | kebabcase | replace "." "-" }}'
    # The component's .NET project name, recorded in .intropy/scaffold.json
    # for workspace-level tooling (e.g. solution file assembly).
    projectName: '{{ .name }}'
    # Name of the sibling shared-contracts project; also drives the dependency
    # output below and the ProjectReference in the skeleton csproj. Plain
    # "Contracts" on purpose: the project is scoped to the system directory it
    # lives in, not to the organization.
    contracts: 'Contracts'
    # The pub/sub component name the skeleton subscribes through
    # (Constants.cs). Recorded in .intropy/scaffold.json for
    # `intropy sys create`, together with the contract parameter above.
    pubsub: 'pubsub'
    # The loader's destination port — the named interface it writes the
    # outside world through. Derived like appId so it stays unique per
    # component. Recorded in .intropy/scaffold.json; `intropy sys create`
    # resolves it to a local file transport by default (external system and
    # transport are never asked for at scaffold time).
    port: '{{ .name | kebabcase | replace "." "-" }}-destination'
  dependencies:
    - template: shared-contracts
      output: '{{ .contracts }}'
      values:
        name: '{{ .contracts }}'
        contract: '{{ .contract }}'
        empty: '{{ .empty }}'

kind: Template
metadata:
  name: extractor
  title: Extractor Integration
  description: Run-to-completion .NET extractor that sweeps a local source folder once per run, runs each file through the Intropy extractor pipeline, and publishes the result as a CloudEvent to a Dapr pub/sub topic.
  tags:
    - example
    - dotnet
    - dapr

    intropy.io/template-level: example
    intropy.io/block-kind: extractor
    intropy.io/data-flow: "in"

  parameters:
    type: object
    required:
      - name
      - organization
      - topic
      - contract

      name:
        type: string
        title: Project name
        description: PascalCase identifier used for the .NET project, root namespace, and assembly. Dot-separated segments are allowed for nested namespaces (e.g. OrderExtractor or Int1055.OrderExtractor).
        pattern: "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*(\\.[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)*$"
      organization:
        type: string
        title: Organization
        description: PascalCase name of the organization the integration runs for. Becomes the telemetry ServiceNamespace and the business-incident source URN (urn:<organization>:<component>).
        pattern: "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$"
      topic:
        type: string
        title: Topic
        description: The pub/sub topic the extractor publishes to. The extractor's half of the system contract — scaffold the consuming loader with the same value.
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      contract:
        type: string
        title: Contract type
        description: PascalCase name of the shared-contracts record the topic carries — the other half of the system contract, recorded in .intropy/scaffold.json for `intropy sys create` to type the topic with. The sample logic uses Order.
        pattern: "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$"
      idempotencyAppId:
        type: string
        title: Idempotency service app-id
        description: Dapr app-id of the Idempotency Service. The default matches the platform-services deployment.
        default: "idempotency-service.services"
      businessIncidentsAppId:
        type: string
        title: Business incident service app-id
        description: Dapr app-id of the Business Incident Service. The default matches the platform-services deployment.
        default: "business-incident-service.services"
      eventSource:
        type: string
        title: CloudEvent source
        description: Envelope `source` (URI) for published events. The default derives as urn:<organization>:<app-id>; set it to preserve an existing event identity during a migration.
        default: ""
      eventType:
        type: string
        title: CloudEvent type
        description: Envelope `type` for published events. The default derives as <organization-lower>.<first-topic-segment>.<last-topic-segment>; set it to preserve an existing event identity during a migration.
        default: ""
      empty:
        type: boolean
        title: Empty bodies
        description: When true, strip sample business logic from pipeline step bodies. The resulting project compiles and starts under Dapr, but every step throws NotImplementedException so a migration agent can fill them in. The idempotency and business-incident wiring stays (the extractor pipeline requires it) with throwing extractor lambdas to replace.
        default: true
  values:
    appId: '{{ .name | kebabcase | replace "." "-" }}'
    # The component's .NET project name, recorded in .intropy/scaffold.json
    # for workspace-level tooling (e.g. solution file assembly).
    projectName: '{{ .name }}'
    # Name of the sibling shared-contracts project; also drives the dependency
    # output below and the ProjectReference in the skeleton csproj. Plain
    # "Contracts" on purpose: the project is scoped to the system directory it
    # lives in, not to the organization.
    contracts: 'Contracts'
    # The pub/sub component name the skeleton publishes through
    # (Constants.cs). Recorded in .intropy/scaffold.json for
    # `intropy sys create`, together with the contract parameter above.
    pubsub: 'pubsub'
    # The extractor's source port — the named interface it reads the outside
    # world through. Derived like appId so it stays unique per component.
    # Recorded in .intropy/scaffold.json; `intropy sys create` resolves it to
    # a local file transport by default (external system and transport are
    # never asked for at scaffold time).
    port: '{{ .name | kebabcase | replace "." "-" }}-source'
    # CloudEvent identity: overridable to preserve an existing identity during a
    # migration; otherwise derived (type: <org>.<first>.<last> of the kebab topic,
    # e.g. product-export -> maxbo.product.export).
    eventSourceValue: '{{ printf "urn:%s:%s" .organization (.name | kebabcase) }}'
    eventTypeValue: '{{ printf "%s.%s.%s" (.organization | lower) (index (regexSplit "-" .topic -1) 0) (index (regexSplit "-" .topic -1) (sub (len (regexSplit "-" .topic -1)) 1)) }}'
  dependencies:
    - template: shared-contracts
      output: '{{ .contracts }}'
      values:
        name: '{{ .contracts }}'
        contract: '{{ .contract }}'
        empty: '{{ .empty }}'

<result>## 1. `internal/template/messageref.go` — the message-ref data model

### What a "message ref" *is*

A message ref is **not** a struct in the values map. It is a single **string parameter** on a template (a bare message id like `io.intropy.maxbo.product.export`, or a full xid `/messagegroups/<gid>/messages/<mid>`) annotated in the manifest with `x-intropy-message-ref: true`. Everything else is *derived at create time* and written into ordinary flat wiring values. Two artifacts come out of resolution:

**(a) The committed trace** — `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/template/messageref.go:19`

```go
type SubscriptionRecord struct {
	Parameter     string `json:"parameter"`               // which template param held the ref
	Message       string `json:"message"`                 // full xid, never a bare id
	SchemaID      string `json:"schemaid,omitempty"`      // from dataschemaxid → schema resource
	SchemaVersion string `json:"schemaVersion,omitempty"` // the schema's *default* version at scaffold time
}
```

Empty schema fields are deliberate: a dangling `dataschemaxid` is kept, not an error ("the record mirrors what the registry actually said").

**(b) The injected wiring values** — flat strings in the values map, using the existing vocabulary from `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/template/wiring.go:14` (`KeyTopic`, `KeyPubsub`, `KeyContract`):

- `topic` and `pubsub` ← `xregistry.SplitChannel(producerEndpoint.Channel)` on `<pubsub>/<topic>`
- `contract` ← *suggested only* from the schema id, and only if unset

### Resolution pipeline

`resolveMessageRefs(t, values, doc, sets, notes)` (messageref.go:129) iterates `messageRefFields(t)` (declaration order) and per param calls `resolveMessageRef` (messageref.go:150):

1. `doc.ResolveMessage(ref)` → `ResolvedMessage{Group, Message, Version}`; a `MessageNotFoundError` is wrapped with `knownMessagesMessage` (close matches by substring, else the whole catalog); ambiguity errors pass through carrying their own remediation.
2. `producerChannel(doc, groupID, messageXid)` (messageref.go:265) → sorted-first producer endpoint's channel split into pubsub/topic. **No producer = hard refusal**: `"message %s has no producer endpoint declared in the registry\ndeclare a producer endpoint for %s before scaffolding a subscriber"`. Sorted-first is called out as "the deterministic pick until the registry grows a way to declare the canonical channel".
3. `injectWiringValue` for `topic` then `pubsub` (messageref.go:190) — the three-way authority rule:
   - absent/empty → set
   - identical → accept silently
   - conflicting **and came from `--set`** → error naming both: `"topic: the registry declares %q for %s, but the values set %q\nchange --set topic= to match the registry, or fix the registry's channel"`
   - conflicting from any other layer (schema default, `spec.values` derivation, values file) → registry wins, noted on stderr: `pubsub: X (from the message registry; was "pubsub")`
4. Schema join: if `Version.DataschemaXid != ""` → `doc.ResolveSchema(...)` → record `SchemaID` + `SchemaVersion`, and call `suggestContract`.

`suggestContract` (messageref.go:213) fills an **unset** `contract` only, with a stderr note (`contract: ProductExport (suggested from the message schema; override with --set contract=<value>)`). A developer-set contract always stands — the doc comment: "the registry names a schema document, not a type".

`SuggestContractName` (messageref.go:232): strip a `.vN` suffix (only when the tail is all digits), split on `-`, Pascal-case each segment. `product-export.v1` → `ProductExport`; `trailing-dot.v` → `TrailingDot.v`.

### Two other exported/notable helpers

- **`PreviewWiring(doc, messageID) MessageWiring`** (messageref.go:284) — read-only "what would this pick inject": pubsub, topic, suggested contract. Touches no values; a message with no resolvable channel returns the zero preview and **no error** (the create flow reports that properly). This is what the dashboard form's routing hint reads.
- **`missingRegistryNote(refs, registryURL, prompter)`** (messageref.go:68) — the interactive-only stderr note when a template offers a subscription and no registry is configured. Returns "" for non-interactive runs, configured registries, or templates without refs.
- **`errNoRegistryConfigured`** (messageref.go:80) and `messageRefValuePresent` — the registry is *mandatory only when a ref actually has a value*.

### What a selected message carries — and what it does NOT

| Concept | Carried? | Where |
|---|---|---|
| topic | yes | values `topic` (injected) |
| pubsub | yes | values `pubsub` (injected) |
| contract | suggestion only | values `contract`, if unset |
| schema id + version | yes | `SubscriptionRecord.SchemaID/SchemaVersion` |
| message xid | yes | `SubscriptionRecord.Message` |
| **CloudEvents type** | **no** | `ResolvedMessage.CloudEventsType()` exists (`internal/xregistry/client.go:117`) but is consumed **only by `int message show`** — nothing injects it into values or the scaffold record |
| **envelope / protocol / datacontenttype** | **no** | read from the model in `message show` only |
| schema document (inlined JSON Schema) | fetched but unused | `SchemaVersion.Document` is decoded and never read by the resolver |

That's a real divergence from plan R4/design step 4 ("plus the CloudEvents type") — see §4.

### `messageref_test.go` (18 KB, table of scenarios)

Fixtures: `subscriberTemplateYAML` (params `name`, `subscription` with `x-intropy-message-ref: true`, `topic`, `contract`; `spec.values: pubsub: 'pubsub'`), `messageRegistryFixture` (one group with producer `perfion-extractor` on `product-distribution-pubsub/sbt-test-product-extractor-001` + a schema `product-export.v1`, and a second group `io.intropy.acme.orders` with **no** producer), `ambiguousRegistryFixture` (same message id in two groups), a `httptest` server serving the doc for any path.

Tests, all end-to-end through `Create`:
- `TestCreateResolvesMessageRef` — rendered `topic=sbt-test-product-extractor-001 pubsub=product-distribution-pubsub contract=ProductExport`; scaffold record has one subscription with parameter/xid/`product-export.v1`@`1`; `scaffold.Values["topic"]` is what system assembly later reads; stderr notes the contract suggestion.
- matching explicit `--set topic=` accepted / conflicting rejected (error must name both values *and* `--set topic=`)
- unknown id → `close matches: io.intropy.acme.orders.placed`
- ambiguous bare id → `matches multiple messages`
- xid form resolves
- no-producer group → refusal naming the gap and the group
- registry unreachable → error contains `resolve message reference` **and the output dir must not exist** (nothing written on a failed resolve)
- `PrepareCreate` without a registry URL but with a ref value → refuses, error mentions `--registry-url` (the dashboard path; asserts "never render with the raw message id as the value")
- template without refs + unroutable registry URL → must not even dial
- developer's `contract=MyOwnContract` stands
- ref *unused* + registry down → succeeds, stderr `warning: message registry unavailable`, zero subscriptions
- `TestCreateMessageRefOverridesDerivedPubsub` — the `spec.values` `pubsub: 'pubsub'` convention yields to the registry with the exact note text
- `TestMissingRegistryNote`, `TestSuggestContractName` (unit)

---

## 2. How message-ref fields are declared in templates

### Param type / field kind — `internal/template/manifest.go`

Two extension keys, both CLI-owned, both inert to JSON Schema tooling:

```go
const MessageRefExtension = "x-intropy-message-ref"   // manifest.go:245
const DerivedExtension    = "x-intropy-derived"       // manifest.go:249
```

`FieldSpec` (manifest.go:189) carries four CLI-only fields alongside the schema ones (`Name/Title/Description/Type/Enum/Default/Pattern/Required`):

```go
Suggestions []string                 `json:"suggestions,omitempty"` // workspace/registry candidates
MessageRef  bool                     `json:"messageRef,omitempty"`  // x-intropy-message-ref
Derived     bool                     `json:"derived,omitempty"`     // x-intropy-derived
Wiring      map[string]MessageWiring `json:"wiring,omitempty"`      // per-message-id preview

type MessageWiring struct {  // manifest.go:235
	Topic    string `json:"topic,omitempty"`
	Pubsub   string `json:"pubsub,omitempty"`
	Contract string `json:"contract,omitempty"`
}
```

`fieldFromSchema` (manifest.go:274) reads both booleans. `validateMessageRefParams` (manifest.go:378) rejects the annotation on any parameter whose `type` is not `"string"` — reported at `LoadTemplate` time. The parameter's *type stays `string`* and value validation never sees the annotation.

The real subscriber shape (from the plan's U5/U7 notes, landed in `intropy-templates` on branch `feat/loader-message-ref`, not this repo): loader gains an optional `subscription` param with `x-intropy-message-ref`, `topic`/`contract` get `x-intropy-derived` and leave `required`, and a top-level `anyOf` guard keeps one of the two flows mandatory:

```yaml
anyOf:
  - required: [subscription]
  - required: [topic, contract]
```

### Derived params — commit 875d1cf6 "registry-expanded parameters"

"Registry-expanded parameters" = the parameters a message-ref resolution *computes* (`topic`, `contract`, and in effect `pubsub`). The commit's thesis: **the message is the subscription; the topic is routing the registry dictates**, so those params stop being asked for and become derived outputs with exactly one author. Concretely, `Derived` changes *who is asked*, not what exists:

- Still a declared parameter — rendering and schema validation see it, an explicit `--set` still applies (the escape hatch).
- **Never prompted**: `missingRequired` (values.go:389) skips `f.Derived` — "schema validation is the backstop when a manifest wrongly leaves it unfillable". Pinned by `TestResolveNeverPromptsDerivedRequired`.
- **Signals "manual path taken"**: `manualWiringChosen` (values.go:289) — any valued derived param cancels the message-ref prompt entirely.
- **Dashboard**: `useTemplateFields.ts` filters `f.derived` out of the inputs when a message is picked, *and strips them from `submitValues`* so a workspace-prefilled seed can never fight the expansion.

### Value resolution — `internal/template/values.go`

`ResolveOptions` (values.go:53) layers: schema defaults → `Base` → `Files` (`-` = stdin, once) → `Sets` → facts prefill → prompts. New field for this feature:

```go
// MessageRefCandidates is the message registry's catalog, the pick
// list a message-ref parameter prompts with. Empty means the registry
// had no answer ... and the message-ref prompt is skipped rather than
// asking for an id from memory.
MessageRefCandidates []string
```

`ResolveWith` order (values.go:102): defaults → base → files → sets → `candidatesByArity`/`applyPrefill` → `promptForMissingRequired` → **`promptForMessageRefs`** → `validateSchema` → `renderDerivedValues` (`spec.values`).

`promptForMessageRefs` (values.go:261) — offered last, after required prompts, with **three cancel conditions**: nil prompter (non-interactive), empty catalog, or `manualWiringChosen`. Enter/empty answer leaves the value unset and defers the verdict to schema validation.

Also new in values.go: `rewriteAnyOfFailure` / `onlyAnyOfFailed` / `requiredCombinations` / `joinAnd` (values.go:432-497) — a *sole* failed top-level `anyOf` is restated as `"the template requires either subscription, or topic and contract"` instead of the jsonschema library's `anyOf/0/required` pointer text. A run that also broke a parameter's own pattern keeps the library's message.

### Prompting — `internal/template/prompt.go`

`StdinPrompter.Prompt` routes suggestions-without-enum to `promptSuggested` (prompt.go:61). The message-ref change is the **required/optional split**:

```go
func (p *StdinPrompter) promptSuggested(f FieldSpec) (any, bool, error) {
	if len(f.Suggestions) == 1 && f.Required {   // <- && f.Required is new
		... shown-default path
	}
	return p.promptSuggestedList(f)
}
```

An optional field *always* renders as a numbered list (however short) and prints `or type a new value; Enter skips`; empty input returns `f.Default` rather than re-prompting. Rationale in the comment: a single-message catalog promoted to a shown default would silently turn Enter from "skip" into "accept". The list still accepts a free-typed novel value (validated by `validateScalar`).

### Facts — `internal/template/facts.go`

`facts.go` is **untouched by this feature** (the only working-tree change is a trailing-newline removal). It remains the *workspace*-derived suggestion index: `TopicKey{Pubsub, Name}`, `Ports`, private `organization` + `contracts map[TopicKey]string` with the "conflicted fact is no fact" rule, built by `BuildWorkspaceFacts` from `WorkspaceFactEntry{BlockKind, Values}`. It matters here as the *contrast*: facts propose (prefill + prompt suggestions, always overridable), while the registry *dictates* topic/pubsub. `suggest.go`'s `suggestField` knows only `organization`/`topic`/`pubsub`/`contract` from facts; message-ref candidates bypass `Suggest` entirely and are handed in from `create.go` (CLI) or `suggestForDir` (dashboard).

### Wiring it up — `internal/template/create.go`

`CreateOptions.RegistryURL` (create.go:61) with the explicit contract: consulted only when a message-ref param exists, mandatory only when one has a value.

`prepareCreateTemplate` (create.go:185) is the single junction shared by `Create` and `PrepareCreate`:

```go
refs := messageRefFields(tmpl)
var export *xregistry.Export
var fetchErr error
if len(refs) > 0 && opts.RegistryURL != "" {
	export, fetchErr = fetchMessageRegistry(ctx, opts)
	if fetchErr != nil && opts.Stderr != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stderr, "warning: message registry unavailable; subscription suggestions are off (%v)\n", fetchErr)
	}
}
if note := missingRegistryNote(refs, opts.RegistryURL, prompter); note != "" { ... }
```

# Agent Instructions

This project is a .NET loader integration built on the Intropy framework.
An ASP.NET service holds a Dapr subscription on a pub/sub topic; the sidecar
POSTs each delivered message to the subscription endpoint, where it is rebuilt
into a CloudEvent, run through the Intropy loader pipeline, and written as
`{orderId}.json` through a Dapr destination binding.

## Project overview

- Framework: .NET 10
- App type: ASP.NET Dapr subscriber service (long-running; a Deployment in
  production)
- App port: assigned by the system host in development; 8080 in the
  container image
- Subscription endpoint: `POST /events/{{ .topic }}`
  (`src/Endpoints/LoaderEndpoints.cs`), announced to the sidecar via
  `GET /dapr/subscribe`; the ack is the response body's `status` field
  (SUCCESS / RETRY)
- Health endpoint: `GET /healthz`
- App id: `{{ .appId }}`
- Pub/sub component: `pubsub` — provided by the system host; messages are
  published from there
- Topic: `{{ .topic }}` — the loader's half of the system contract; the
  publishing extractor uses the same topic
- Destination port: `{{ .port }}` — the named interface the loader
  writes the outside world through; the system host declares it in
  `Ports.cs` and the Dapr binding uses the same name, resolved to a local
  folder in development. In production the same name resolves to the
  environment's binding (e.g. SFTP) from the deploy overlay's GitOps
  values — rebinding the port is a deployment change, never a code change
- Idempotency Service: reached via Dapr service invocation, app id
  `{{ .idempotencyAppId }}` (from `src/appsettings.json`, overridable per environment)
- Business Incident Service: reached via Dapr service invocation, app id
  `{{ .businessIncidentsAppId }}` (from `src/appsettings.json`, overridable per environment)
- Shared contracts: the consumed contract (`{{ .contract }}`, `OrderLine`) lives in the
  sibling project `../{{ .contracts }}` (namespace `{{ .contracts }}`), referenced
  from `src/{{ .name }}.csproj`. The sibling is scaffolded by this template's
  dependency declaration; when it already exists (another component created
  it) the scaffold leaves it untouched. The destination load record (`Out`)
  stays local in `src/Model/`.

## Important files

- `Taskfile.yml` - build and test tasks (`task build`, `task test`; the
  suites also run separately via `task test:unit` / `task test:integration`).
- `Dockerfile` - multi-stage image build on the chiseled ASP.NET runtime,
  listening on port 8080 in the container
  (`docker build --build-context contracts=../{{ .contracts }} -t {{ .appId }} .` —
  the shared contracts sibling enters as a named context); the image contains
  only the app — the Dapr sidecar and components come from the deployment
  environment.
- `src/Program.cs` - host bootstrap: applies the service registrations from
  `Composition` and maps the endpoints (subscription, `/dapr/subscribe`,
  `/healthz`).
- `src/Composition/Composition.cs` - every service registration (including
  the pipeline and the load edge: the sender is a DI-registered
  `SendStep<Out, Context>` resolved by `BuildPipeline(provider)` like any
  other external). Note the namespace/type collision: `{{ .name }}.Composition`
  is both namespace and class, so call sites inside nested namespaces use the
