### What a "message ref" *is*

A message ref is **not** a struct in the values map. It is a single **string parameter** on a template (a bare message id like `io.intropy.maxbo.product.export`, or a full xid `/messagegroups/<gid>/messages/<mid>`) annotated in the manifest with `x-intropy-message-ref: true`. Everything else is *derived at create time* and written into ordinary flat wiring values. Two artifacts come out of resolution:

**(a) The committed trace** — `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/template/messageref.go:19`

```go
type SubscriptionRecord struct {
	Parameter     string `json:"parameter"`               // which template param held the ref
	Message       string `json:"message"`                 // full xid, never a bare id
	SchemaID      string `json:"schemaid,omitempty"`      // from dataschemaxid → schema resource
	SchemaVersion string `json:"schemaVersion,omitempty"` // the schema's *default* version at scaffold time
}
```

Empty schema fields are deliberate: a dangling `dataschemaxid` is kept, not an error ("the record mirrors what the registry actually said").

**(b) The injected wiring values** — flat strings in the values map, using the existing vocabulary from `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/template/wiring.go:14` (`KeyTopic`, `KeyPubsub`, `KeyContract`):

- `topic` and `pubsub` ← `xregistry.SplitChannel(producerEndpoint.Channel)` on `<pubsub>/<topic>`
- `contract` ← *suggested only* from the schema id, and only if unset

### Resolution pipeline

`resolveMessageRefs(t, values, doc, sets, notes)` (messageref.go:129) iterates `messageRefFields(t)` (declaration order) and per param calls `resolveMessageRef` (messageref.go:150):

1. `doc.ResolveMessage(ref)` → `ResolvedMessage{Group, Message, Version}`; a `MessageNotFoundError` is wrapped with `knownMessagesMessage` (close matches by substring, else the whole catalog); ambiguity errors pass through carrying their own remediation.
2. `producerChannel(doc, groupID, messageXid)` (messageref.go:265) → sorted-first producer endpoint's channel split into pubsub/topic. **No producer = hard refusal**: `"message %s has no producer endpoint declared in the registry\ndeclare a producer endpoint for %s before scaffolding a subscriber"`. Sorted-first is called out as "the deterministic pick until the registry grows a way to declare the canonical channel".
3. `injectWiringValue` for `topic` then `pubsub` (messageref.go:190) — the three-way authority rule:
   - absent/empty → set
   - identical → accept silently
   - conflicting **and came from `--set`** → error naming both: `"topic: the registry declares %q for %s, but the values set %q\nchange --set topic= to match the registry, or fix the registry's channel"`
   - conflicting from any other layer (schema default, `spec.values` derivation, values file) → registry wins, noted on stderr: `pubsub: X (from the message registry; was "pubsub")`
4. Schema join: if `Version.DataschemaXid != ""` → `doc.ResolveSchema(...)` → record `SchemaID` + `SchemaVersion`, and call `suggestContract`.

`suggestContract` (messageref.go:213) fills an **unset** `contract` only, with a stderr note (`contract: ProductExport (suggested from the message schema; override with --set contract=<value>)`). A developer-set contract always stands — the doc comment: "the registry names a schema document, not a type".

`SuggestContractName` (messageref.go:232): strip a `.vN` suffix (only when the tail is all digits), split on `-`, Pascal-case each segment. `product-export.v1` → `ProductExport`; `trailing-dot.v` → `TrailingDot.v`.

- **`missingRegistryNote(refs, registryURL, prompter)`** (messageref.go:68) — the interactive-only stderr note when a template offers a subscription and no registry is configured. Returns "" for non-interactive runs, configured registries, or templates without refs.

| topic | yes | values `topic` (injected) |
| pubsub | yes | values `pubsub` (injected) |
| contract | suggestion only | values `contract`, if unset |
| schema id + version | yes | `SubscriptionRecord.SchemaID/SchemaVersion` |

### Param type / field kind — `internal/template/manifest.go`

Two extension keys, both CLI-owned, both inert to JSON Schema tooling:

```go

const DerivedExtension    = "x-intropy-derived"       // manifest.go:249
```

`FieldSpec` (manifest.go:189) carries four CLI-only fields alongside the schema ones (`Name/Title/Description/Type/Enum/Default/Pattern/Required`):

```go

MessageRef  bool                     `json:"messageRef,omitempty"`  // x-intropy-message-ref
Derived     bool                     `json:"derived,omitempty"`     // x-intropy-derived
Wiring      map[string]MessageWiring `json:"wiring,omitempty"`      // per-message-id preview

type MessageWiring struct {  // manifest.go:235
	Topic    string `json:"topic,omitempty"`
```

`fieldFromSchema` (manifest.go:274) reads both booleans. `validateMessageRefParams` (manifest.go:378) rejects the annotation on any parameter whose `type` is not `"string"` — reported at `LoadTemplate` time. The parameter's *type stays `string`* and value validation never sees the annotation.

The real subscriber shape (from the plan's U5/U7 notes, landed in `intropy-templates` on branch `feat/loader-message-ref`, not this repo): loader gains an optional `subscription` param with `x-intropy-message-ref`, `topic`/`contract` get `x-intropy-derived` and leave `required`, and a top-level `anyOf` guard keeps one of the two flows mandatory:

```yaml
anyOf:
  - required: [subscription]
  - required: [topic, contract]
```

### Derived params — commit 875d1cf6 "registry-expanded parameters"

"Registry-expanded parameters" = the parameters a message-ref resolution *computes* (`topic`, `contract`, and in effect `pubsub`). The commit's thesis: **the message is the subscription; the topic is routing the registry dictates**, so those params stop being asked for and become derived outputs with exactly one author. Concretely, `Derived` changes *who is asked*, not what exists:

- Still a declared parameter — rendering and schema validation see it, an explicit `--set` still applies (the escape hatch).
- **Never prompted**: `missingRequired` (values.go:389) skips `f.Derived` — "schema validation is the backstop when a manifest wrongly leaves it unfillable". Pinned by `TestResolveNeverPromptsDerivedRequired`.
- **Signals "manual path taken"**: `manualWiringChosen` (values.go:289) — any valued derived param cancels the message-ref prompt entirely.
- **Dashboard**: `useTemplateFields.ts` filters `f.derived` out of the inputs when a message is picked, *and strips them from `submitValues`* so a workspace-prefilled seed can never fight the expansion.

### Value resolution — `internal/template/values.go`

`ResolveOptions` (values.go:53) layers: schema defaults → `Base` → `Files` (`-` = stdin, once) → `Sets` → facts prefill → prompts. New field for this feature:

```go
// MessageRefCandidates is the message registry's catalog, the pick
// list a message-ref parameter prompts with. Empty means the registry
// had no answer ... and the message-ref prompt is skipped rather than
// asking for an id from memory.
MessageRefCandidates []string
```

`ResolveWith` order (values.go:102): defaults → base → files → sets → `candidatesByArity`/`applyPrefill` → `promptForMissingRequired` → **`promptForMessageRefs`** → `validateSchema` → `renderDerivedValues` (`spec.values`).

`promptForMessageRefs` (values.go:261) — offered last, after required prompts, with **three cancel conditions**: nil prompter (non-interactive), empty catalog, or `manualWiringChosen`. Enter/empty answer leaves the value unset and defers the verdict to schema validation.

Also new in values.go: `rewriteAnyOfFailure` / `onlyAnyOfFailed` / `requiredCombinations` / `joinAnd` (values.go:432-497) — a *sole* failed top-level `anyOf` is restated as `"the template requires either subscription, or topic and contract"` instead of the jsonschema library's `anyOf/0/required` pointer text. A run that also broke a parameter's own pattern keeps the library's message.

### Prompting — `internal/template/prompt.go`

`StdinPrompter.Prompt` routes suggestions-without-enum to `promptSuggested` (prompt.go:61). The message-ref change is the **required/optional split**:

```go
func (p *StdinPrompter) promptSuggested(f FieldSpec) (any, bool, error) {
	if len(f.Suggestions) == 1 && f.Required {   // <- && f.Required is new
		... shown-default path
	}
	return p.promptSuggestedList(f)
}
```

An optional field *always* renders as a numbered list (however short) and prints `or type a new value; Enter skips`; empty input returns `f.Default` rather than re-prompting. Rationale in the comment: a single-message catalog promoted to a shown default would silently turn Enter from "skip" into "accept". The list still accepts a free-typed novel value (validated by `validateScalar`).

### Facts — `internal/template/facts.go`

`facts.go` is **untouched by this feature** (the only working-tree change is a trailing-newline removal). It remains the *workspace*-derived suggestion index: `TopicKey{Pubsub, Name}`, `Ports`, private `organization` + `contracts map[TopicKey]string` with the "conflicted fact is no fact" rule, built by `BuildWorkspaceFacts` from `WorkspaceFactEntry{BlockKind, Values}`. It matters here as the *contrast*: facts propose (prefill + prompt suggestions, always overridable), while the registry *dictates* topic/pubsub. `suggest.go`'s `suggestField` knows only `organization`/`topic`/`pubsub`/`contract` from facts; message-ref candidates bypass `Suggest` entirely and are handed in from `create.go` (CLI) or `suggestForDir` (dashboard).

### Wiring it up — `internal/template/create.go`

`CreateOptions.RegistryURL` (create.go:61) with the explicit contract: consulted only when a message-ref param exists, mandatory only when one has a value.

`prepareCreateTemplate` (create.go:185) is the single junction shared by `Create` and `PrepareCreate`:

```go
var export *xregistry.Export
```

## 3. The xregistry client / registry layer

### `internal/xregistry/types.go` — the message document

Package doc is explicit that this is unrelated to `internal/registry` (the OCI client). The document is `GET /export`, "byte-identical to `GET /?doc&inline=*,capabilities,modelsource`".

```go
type Export struct {
	RegistryID, Name, Description string
	MessageGroups map[string]*MessageGroup `json:"messagegroups"`
	SchemaGroups  map[string]*SchemaGroup  `json:"schemagroups"`
	Endpoints     map[string]*Endpoint     `json:"endpoints"`
}

type MessageGroup struct { MessageGroupID, Xid, Name, Description, Envelope, Protocol string
                           Messages map[string]*Message `json:"messages"` }

type Message struct { MessageID, Xid, Name, Description string
                      Versions map[string]*MessageVersion `json:"versions"` }

type MessageVersion struct {
	VersionID string; IsDefault bool
	Name, Description string
	Envelope         string
	EnvelopeMetadata map[string]EnvelopeAttr `json:"envelopemetadata"`
	Protocol         string
	DataschemaFormat string
	DataschemaXid    string   // "/schemagroups/<gid>/schemas/<sid>" — no /versions suffix
	Datacontenttype  string
}

type EnvelopeAttr struct { Value json.RawMessage; Type string; Required bool; Description string }
```

The load-bearing shape fact (found by live smoke, per the plan notes): **in the export's document view a resource carries only its own attributes — everything a subscriber needs lives on the default version.** Hence `Message.DefaultVersion()` / `Schema.DefaultVersion()` (isdefault wins; a single-version resource falls back to it) and the `ResolvedMessage.DisplayName/DisplayDescription` accessors that hide the split.

`Endpoint` is the exception — no versions, attributes on the entity itself: `Usage []string`, `Channel string` (`"<pubsub>/<topic>"`), `MessageGroups []string` (xid refs).

`SchemaVersion.Document json.RawMessage \`json:"schema"\`` holds the inlined JSON Schema (present because /export inlines everything; currently unread by the CLI).

### `internal/xregistry/client.go` — fetch + joins

- `NewClient(baseURL, ...Option)` — absolute URL required (error text suggests `https://registry.example.com`), trailing slash trimmed; `WithHTTPClient`, `WithUserAgent`.
- `Export(ctx)` — `GET {base}/export`, **explicit `Accept: application/json`** ("the registry negotiates HTML vs JSON on Accept, and only a client that asks for JSON specifically is immune to future portal routes"); non-200 → `get export from %s: registry returned %s`; parse failure distinct. Read-only by design: "every write verb there answers 405".
- `ResolvedMessage{Group, Message, Version}` + `DisplayName`, `DisplayDescription`, `CloudEventsType()` (fixed value of the `type` envelope attribute, "by registry convention equals the message id").
- `ResolveMessage(ref)` — xid path (`resolveXid`, strict 4-segment `/messagegroups/<g>/messages/<m>`) or bare id scanned across all groups: 0 → `MessageNotFoundError`, 1 → hit, >1 → `AmbiguousMessageError{Ref, Xids}` with `"use a full xid: ..."`.
- `ResolveSchema(xid)` — strict 4-segment `/schemagroups/<g>/schemas/<s>`; malformed **or** dangling both → `SchemaNotFoundError`, "never a panic: the registry keeps unresolved references with a warning, so clients meet them in the wild".
- `ProducerEndpointsFor(groupID)` — endpoints with `usage` containing `"producer"` whose `messagegroups` contains `/messagegroups/<gid>`, sorted by endpoint id. Empty is not an error — an authoring gap the caller surfaces.
- `SplitChannel(channel)` → `strings.Cut(channel, "/")`, both halves non-empty, else `channel %q is not <pubsub>/<topic>`.

A message ref is **not** a struct in the values map. 	SchemaVersion string `json:"schemaVersion,omitempty"` // the schema's *default* version at scaffold time

Empty schema fields are deliberate: a dangling `dataschemaxid` is kept, not an error ("the record mirrors what the registry actually said").


### Derived params — commit 875d1cf6 "registry-expanded parameters"

"Registry-expanded parameters" = the parameters a message-ref resolution *computes* (`topic`, `contract`, and in effect `pubsub`). The commit's thesis: **the message is the subscription; the topic is routing the registry dictates**, so those params stop being asked for and become derived outputs with exactly one author. Concretely, `Derived` changes *who is asked*, not what exists:

- Still a declared parameter — rendering and schema validation see it, an explicit `--set` still applies (the escape hatch).
- **Never prompted**: `missingRequired` (values.go:389) skips `f.Derived` — "schema validation is the backstop when a manifest wrongly leaves it unfillable". Pinned by `TestResolveNeverPromptsDerivedRequired`.

`ResolveOptions` (values.go:53) layers: schema defaults → `Base` → `Files` (`-` = stdin, once) → `Sets` → facts prefill → prompts. New field for this feature:

```go

// list a message-ref parameter prompts with. Empty means the registry
// had no answer ... and the message-ref prompt is skipped rather than
// asking for an id from memory.
```

`ResolveWith` order (values.go:102): defaults → base → files → sets → `candidatesByArity`/`applyPrefill` → `promptForMissingRequired` → **`promptForMessageRefs`** → `validateSchema` → `renderDerivedValues` (`spec.values`).

`promptForMessageRefs` (values.go:261) — offered last, after required prompts, with **three cancel conditions**: nil prompter (non-interactive), empty catalog, or `manualWiringChosen`. Enter/empty answer leaves the value unset and defers the verdict to schema validation.

### Prompting — `internal/template/prompt.go`

`StdinPrompter.Prompt` routes suggestions-without-enum to `promptSuggested` (prompt.go:61). The message-ref change is the **required/optional split**:

```go
func (p *StdinPrompter) promptSuggested(f FieldSpec) (any, bool, error) {
	if len(f.Suggestions) == 1 && f.Required {   // <- && f.Required is new
		... shown-default path

}
```

An optional field *always* renders as a numbered list (however short) and prints `or type a new value; Enter skips`; empty input returns `f.Default` rather than re-prompting. Rationale in the comment: a single-message catalog promoted to a shown default would silently turn Enter from "skip" into "accept". The list still accepts a free-typed novel value (validated by `validateScalar`).

`facts.go` is **untouched by this feature** (the only working-tree change is a trailing-newline removal). It remains the *workspace*-derived suggestion index: `TopicKey{Pubsub, Name}`, `Ports`, private `organization` + `contracts map[TopicKey]string` with the "conflicted fact is no fact" rule, built by `BuildWorkspaceFacts` from `WorkspaceFactEntry{BlockKind, Values}`. `CreateOptions.RegistryURL` (create.go:61) with the explicit contract: consulted only when a message-ref param exists, mandatory only when one has a value.

`prepareCreateTemplate` (create.go:185) is the single junction shared by `Create` and `PrepareCreate`:

```go
var export *xregistry.Export
```

## 3. The xregistry client / registry layer

### `internal/xregistry/types.go` — the message document

Package doc is explicit that this is unrelated to `internal/registry` (the OCI client). The document is `GET /export`, "byte-identical to `GET /?doc&inline=*,capabilities,modelsource`".

```go
type Export struct {
	RegistryID, Name, Description string
	MessageGroups map[string]*MessageGroup `json:"messagegroups"`
	SchemaGroups  map[string]*SchemaGroup  `json:"schemagroups"`
	Endpoints     map[string]*Endpoint     `json:"endpoints"`
}

type MessageGroup struct { MessageGroupID, Xid, Name, Description, Envelope, Protocol string
                           Messages map[string]*Message `json:"messages"` }

type Message struct { MessageID, Xid, Name, Description string
                      Versions map[string]*MessageVersion `json:"versions"` }

type MessageVersion struct {
	VersionID string; IsDefault bool
	Name, Description string
	Envelope         string
	EnvelopeMetadata map[string]EnvelopeAttr `json:"envelopemetadata"`
	Protocol         string
	DataschemaFormat string
	DataschemaXid    string   // "/schemagroups/<gid>/schemas/<sid>" — no /versions suffix
	Datacontenttype  string
}

type EnvelopeAttr struct { Value json.RawMessage; Type string; Required bool; Description string }
```

The load-bearing shape fact (found by live smoke, per the plan notes): **in the export's document view a resource carries only its own attributes — everything a subscriber needs lives on the default version.** Hence `Message.DefaultVersion()` / `Schema.DefaultVersion()` (isdefault wins; a single-version resource falls back to it) and the `ResolvedMessage.DisplayName/DisplayDescription` accessors that hide the split.

`Endpoint` is the exception — no versions, attributes on the entity itself: `Usage []string`, `Channel string` (`"<pubsub>/<topic>"`), `MessageGroups []string` (xid refs).

`SchemaVersion.Document json.RawMessage \`json:"schema"\`` holds the inlined JSON Schema (present because /export inlines everything; currently unread by the CLI).

### `internal/xregistry/client.go` — fetch + joins

- `NewClient(baseURL, ...Option)` — absolute URL required (error text suggests `https://registry.example.com`), trailing slash trimmed; `WithHTTPClient`, `WithUserAgent`.
- `Export(ctx)` — `GET {base}/export`, **explicit `Accept: application/json`** ("the registry negotiates HTML vs JSON on Accept, and only a client that asks for JSON specifically is immune to future portal routes"); non-200 → `get export from %s: registry returned %s`; parse failure distinct. Read-only by design: "every write verb there answers 405".
- `ResolvedMessage{Group, Message, Version}` + `DisplayName`, `DisplayDescription`, `CloudEventsType()` (fixed value of the `type` envelope attribute, "by registry convention equals the message id").
- `ResolveMessage(ref)` — xid path (`resolveXid`, strict 4-segment `/messagegroups/<g>/messages/<m>`) or bare id scanned across all groups: 0 → `MessageNotFoundError`, 1 → hit, >1 → `AmbiguousMessageError{Ref, Xids}` with `"use a full xid: ..."`.
- `ResolveSchema(xid)` — strict 4-segment `/schemagroups/<g>/schemas/<s>`; malformed **or** dangling both → `SchemaNotFoundError`, "never a panic: the registry keeps unresolved references with a warning, so clients meet them in the wild".
- `ProducerEndpointsFor(groupID)` — endpoints with `usage` containing `"producer"` whose `messagegroups` contains `/messagegroups/<gid>`, sorted by endpoint id. Empty is not an error — an authoring gap the caller surfaces.

```go
type Topology struct {
	APIVersion string      `json:"apiVersion"`   // "topology.intropy.io/v1"
	Kind       string      `json:"kind,omitempty"` // "SystemTopology"
	System     string      `json:"system"`
	Components []Component `json:"components,omitempty"`
	Topics     []Topic     `json:"topics,omitempty"`

	Contracts  []Contract  `json:"contracts,omitempty"`

	MediaType   string          `json:"mediaType,omitempty"`
	Fingerprint string          `json:"fingerprint,omitempty"`

```

The comment on `Contract.Schema` states the boundary plainly: *"Schema is the contract's JSON Schema as the host emitted it; the CLI passes it through to the frontend without interpreting it."* `Decode` (line 159) rejects any other `apiVersion` rather than guessing. `Contracts` may legitimately be nil (`TestDecodeWithoutContracts`, `topology_test.go:132` — "host predates the registry").

```go
for _, c := range topo.Contracts {
    if c.Name == t.Contract && c.ShortName != "" {
```

`joinTopology` (line 185) joins a component to the graph **by directory name**, producing `publishes[]`/`subscribes[]` as `ContractEdge`s with `publishers`/`subscribers` riding along. `GraphStatus` is one of `matched | no-topology | not-in-graph | topology-error | pending`.

```go
// SplitChannel splits an endpoint channel into its pubsub component and
// topic. The registry's naming convention is "<pubsub>/<topic>" — the same
// two values the CLI's wiring vocabulary records separately.
func SplitChannel(channel string) (pubsub, topic string, err error) {
	pubsub, topic, ok := strings.Cut(channel, "/")
	if !ok || pubsub == "" || topic == "" {
		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("channel %q is not <pubsub>/<topic>", channel)
	}
	return pubsub, topic, nil
```
```go
}
```

```go
// SplitChannel splits an endpoint channel into its pubsub component and
// topic. The registry's naming convention is "<pubsub>/<topic>" — the same
// two values the CLI's wiring vocabulary records separately.
func SplitChannel(channel string) (pubsub, topic string, err error) {
	pubsub, topic, ok := strings.Cut(channel, "/")
	if !ok || pubsub == "" || topic == "" {
		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("channel %q is not <pubsub>/<topic>", channel)
	}
	return pubsub, topic, nil
```
```go
}
```

# 4. What "contract" means as a template parameter

## The vocabulary constant

`/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/template/wiring.go:14`:
```go
const (
	KeyAppID = "appId"; KeyTopic = "topic"; KeyContract = "contract"
	KeyPubsub = "pubsub"; KeyPort = "port"; KeyFromPort = "fromPort"; KeyToPort = "toPort"
	KeyName = "name"; KeyOrganization = "organization"
	KeyProjectName = "projectName"; KeySystemClass = "systemClass"
	DefaultPubsub = "pubsub"
)
```
The file's own doc comment is explicit: *"They are CLI-owned convention, not manifest schema — a template that names its parameters otherwise simply gets no assembly or suggestions."*

## Semantics

`contract` is the **PascalCase C# type name of the record a topic's messages carry** — the shared-contracts `record` type. It is the join key between the two halves of one topic: the publishing extractor and the subscribing loader must record the same `contract` for the same `TopicKey`, or `Assemble` refuses.

## "Required, never defaulted" — confirmed, with nuance

| Template | `contract` | required? | default? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `extractor` | `type: string`, `pattern: ^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$` | **yes** (in `required:`) | **none** |
| `loader` | same pattern, plus `x-intropy-derived: true` | **yes via `anyOf`**: `[{required:[subscription]}, {required:[topic, contract]}]` | **none** |
| `shared-contracts` | same pattern | **no** | **`Order`** |
| `transactional` | absent entirely | — | — |

So: in every **component/block** template `contract` is required and carries **no default**. The only default lives in `shared-contracts`, where the component template always overrides it by passing its own value down through `spec.dependencies[].values.contract`. There is also **no CLI-side default** — `internal/template/suggest.go` only ever *suggests* it, and `applyPrefill` only fires on a workspace fact with exactly one candidate, always announced on stderr.

Three ways `contract` can arrive without being typed, all announced:
1. **Workspace prefill** (`applyPrefill`, values.go:167) — one candidate, note: `contract: Order (from workspace; override with --set contract=<value>)`.
2. **Prompt suggestion** — narrowed by the already-confirmed `topic` via `facts.ContractFor(TopicKey{...})` (suggest.go:68-82); the prompter's confirmation is the value.
3. **Message-registry suggestion** — `suggestContract` (messageref.go:213) fills an **unset** contract from the resolved schema id via `SuggestContractName` (`"product-export.v1"` → `"ProductExport"`), noted on stderr. Crucially asymmetric with `topic`/`pubsub`: `injectWiringValue` lets the registry **override** a non-`--set` topic/pubsub (the registry owns routing), whereas *"The contract is different — it is developer-owned (the registry names a schema document, not a type), so a present contract always stands and the registry only fills a gap."*

`Assemble` (line 22) per entry:
- `Role == RoleSharedLibrary` → `SharedLibrary{Path, Name: values.name}`, **not** a component. >1 is a hard error; 0 is legal.
- `Role == RoleSystemHost` → skipped ("an existing system host").
- `BlockKind == ""` → skipped with "re-scaffold with a newer template release".
- kind not in `blockParsers` → skipped, naming the supported kinds.

Cross-component invariants enforced here (not in parsers):

- duplicate port → error ("each block gets its own port")
- same `TopicKey` with **conflicting contracts** → error naming both contracts and both dirs

## Where the edges actually get derived

The CLI supplies **raw names**; the template derives field identifiers and joins. `system-host/skeleton/{{ .systemClass }}.cs.tmpl` builds two lookup dicts (`$topicField` keyed `"<pubsub>/<name>"`, `$portField` keyed by port name), field name = `regexReplaceAll "[-._]" name " " | title | replace " " ""`, then:

```
extractor:                 builder.AddExtractor(appId)[.From(Ports.X)].Publishes(Topics.Y).Uses(Idempotency).Uses(BusinessIncidents);
transactional-integration: builder.AddTransactionalIntegration(appId).From(Ports.A).To(Ports.B).Uses(...).Uses(...);
loader (else branch):      builder.AddLoader(appId).Subscribes(Topics.Y)[.To(Ports.X)].Uses(...).Uses(...);
```

`Topics.cs.tmpl` and `Ports.cs.tmpl` each `fail` the render on a **field-name collision** (two topics/ports deriving the same C# identifier), naming both. `Topics.cs.tmpl` also honors an optional per-topic `contractNamespace` (for adopted components whose contract lives in a sub-namespace).

## Prompt-time facts (the other consumer)

`internal/system/facts.go` → `LoadWorkspaceFacts` / `WorkspaceFactsOf` (drops `BlockKind == ""` records) → `template.BuildWorkspaceFacts` in `internal/template/facts.go:104`.

`WorkspaceFacts` holds `TopicKeys []TopicKey`, `Ports []string`, private `organization`, private `contracts map[TopicKey]string`. It is deliberately **lenient** where `Assemble` is strict (`SoftValue` vs `RecordValue`) — a suggestion aid must never fail a create. Conflict rule: conflicting contracts on one topic key, or conflicting organizations, **demote the fact to absent** rather than guess.

`internal/template/suggest.go` — `Suggest` is the CLI-owned convention registry keyed on parameter *name*: `organization`, `topic`, `pubsub`, `contract`. **Ports are deliberately excluded** — an already-taken port name is an *anti*-suggestion, since assembly rejects a shared port. `dropDefaultCandidate` prevents a suggestion competing with the schema default bracket.

## `sys update` (adding a component to an existing system)

`internal/system/update.go` + `cmd/intropy/sys_update.go`: locates the host, uses the **host record's stored `values` as the baseline** (never a re-scan), finds "orphans" (assemblable scaffolds the record doesn't declare), merges `components`, re-renders via `RenderUpdate` with three-way outcomes, and rewrites the record **last** — never on a conflict. `Kept` reports declared components whose scaffold has disappeared.

# 4. What "contract" means as a template parameter

## The vocabulary constant

`/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/template/wiring.go:14`:
```go
const (
	KeyAppID = "appId"; KeyTopic = "topic"; KeyContract = "contract"
	KeyPubsub = "pubsub"; KeyPort = "port"; KeyFromPort = "fromPort"; KeyToPort = "toPort"
	KeyName = "name"; KeyOrganization = "organization"
	KeyProjectName = "projectName"; KeySystemClass = "systemClass"
	DefaultPubsub = "pubsub"
)
```
The file's own doc comment is explicit: *"They are CLI-owned convention, not manifest schema — a template that names its parameters otherwise simply gets no assembly or suggestions."*

## Semantics

`contract` is the **PascalCase C# type name of the record a topic's messages carry** — the shared-contracts `record` type. It is the join key between the two halves of one topic: the publishing extractor and the subscribing loader must record the same `contract` for the same `TopicKey`, or `Assemble` refuses.

## "Required, never defaulted" — confirmed, with nuance

| Template | `contract` | required? | default? |

| `extractor` | `type: string`, `pattern: ^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$` | **yes** (in `required:`) | **none** |

# 4. What "contract" means as a template parameter

## The vocabulary constant

`/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/template/wiring.go:14`:
```go
const (
	KeyAppID = "appId"; KeyTopic = "topic"; KeyContract = "contract"
	KeyPubsub = "pubsub"; KeyPort = "port"; KeyFromPort = "fromPort"; KeyToPort = "toPort"
	KeyName = "name"; KeyOrganization = "organization"
	KeyProjectName = "projectName"; KeySystemClass = "systemClass"
	DefaultPubsub = "pubsub"
)
```
The file's own doc comment is explicit: *"They are CLI-owned convention, not manifest schema — a template that names its parameters otherwise simply gets no assembly or suggestions."*

## Semantics

`contract` is the **PascalCase C# type name of the record a topic's messages carry** — the shared-contracts `record` type. It is the join key between the two halves of one topic: the publishing extractor and the subscribing loader must record the same `contract` for the same `TopicKey`, or `Assemble` refuses.

## "Required, never defaulted" — confirmed, with nuance

| Template | `contract` | required? | default? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `extractor` | `type: string`, `pattern: ^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$` | **yes** (in `required:`) | **none** |
| `loader` | same pattern, plus `x-intropy-derived: true` | **yes via `anyOf`**: `[{required:[subscription]}, {required:[topic, contract]}]` | **none** |
| `shared-contracts` | same pattern | **no** | **`Order`** |
| `transactional` | absent entirely | — | — |

So: in every **component/block** template `contract` is required and carries **no default**. The only default lives in `shared-contracts`, where the component template always overrides it by passing its own value down through `spec.dependencies[].values.contract`. There is also **no CLI-side default** — `internal/template/suggest.go` only ever *suggests* it, and `applyPrefill` only fires on a workspace fact with exactly one candidate, always announced on stderr.

Three ways `contract` can arrive without being typed, all announced:
1. **Workspace prefill** (`applyPrefill`, values.go:167) — one candidate, note: `contract: Order (from workspace; override with --set contract=<value>)`.
2. **Prompt suggestion** — narrowed by the already-confirmed `topic` via `facts.ContractFor(TopicKey{...})` (suggest.go:68-82); the prompter's confirmation is the value.
3. **Message-registry suggestion** — `suggestContract` (messageref.go:213) fills an **unset** contract from the resolved schema id via `SuggestContractName` (`"product-export.v1"` → `"ProductExport"`), noted on stderr. Crucially asymmetric with `topic`/`pubsub`: `injectWiringValue` lets the registry **override** a non-`--set` topic/pubsub (the registry owns routing), whereas *"The contract is different — it is developer-owned (the registry names a schema document, not a type), so a present contract always stands and the registry only fills a gap."*

- `extractor/skeleton/src/Model/Source{{ .contract }}.cs.tmpl` → `src/Model/SourceOrder.cs`

- `src/Process/Validator.cs`: `BusinessStepResult<Source{{ .contract }}>`
- `src/Process/Transformer.cs`: `TransformStep<Source{{ .contract }}, {{ .contract }}, Context>`, `new {{ .contract }}(...)`, `TechnicalStepResult<{{ .contract }}>`
- `src/Composition/Composition.cs`: `Extractor<Source{{ .contract }}, {{ .contract }}, Context> BuildPipeline(...)`, `CloudEventSerializeStep<{{ .contract }}, Context>`
- `test/…Test.Integration/FakeEdges.cs`: `Extractor<Source{{ .contract }}, {{ .contract }}, Context> BuildPipeline(...)`
- all unit tests

**In C# type positions** (loader):
- `src/Process/Deserializer.cs`: `class Deserializer : DeserializeStep<{{ .contract }}, Context>`, `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<{{ .contract }}>`
- `src/Composition/Composition.cs`: `LoaderBuilder<{{ .contract }}, Out, Context>.Create(...)`, `Loader<{{ .contract }}, Out, Context> BuildPipeline(...)`
- `src/Endpoints/LoaderEndpoints.cs`: `[FromServices] Loader<{{ .contract }}, Out, Context> pipeline`

**In the shared library**: `shared-contracts/skeleton/{{ .contract }}.cs.tmpl` emits the `record {{ .contract }}(...)` itself (empty shell when `empty: true`).

**In the system host** (via `sys create`, `topics[].contract`): `Topics.cs.tmpl` renders
```csharp

```
and `system-host`'s own `spec.dependencies` uses `contract: '{{ (index .topics 0).contract }}'` to scaffold `Contracts/` when the workspace lacks a shared library.

**Not** `contract`: the sibling **project/namespace** name is a separate derived value `contracts: 'Contracts'` (`spec.values`), used for `using {{ .contracts }};`, the `ProjectReference Include="../../{{ .contracts }}/{{ .contracts }}.csproj"`, the Dockerfile build context, and `dependencies[].output`. `contract` = the type; `contracts` = the project. Easy to conflate.

## The error message that pins the requirement

`internal/system/blocks.go:45`:
```go

if err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("%w\nRe-scaffold this integration with a template release that records the contract type, or add \"contract\": \"<TypeName>\" to the record's values", err)
```

## Established context (verified — do not re-derive, but do read the named files)

The CLI can already resolve a "message ref": a template parameter annotated `x-intropy-message-ref: true` holds an xRegistry message id. At `int create` time, `internal/template/messageref.go` `resolveMessageRef` resolves it against a single `GET /export` document (`internal/xregistry/{client,types}.go`) and injects `topic` + `pubsub` into the values map, records a `SubscriptionRecord{Parameter, Message(xid), SchemaID, SchemaVersion}` into `.intropy/scaffold.json` (`internal/template/scaffold.go`), and *suggests* a `contract` type name via `SuggestContractName` ("product-export.v1" → "ProductExport").

Critically: `xregistry.SchemaVersion.Document json.RawMessage` (json tag `schema`) already holds the **inlined JSON Schema document** from /export. Nothing reads it. That is the input to this work.

A real schema (from ~/dev/intropy/intropy-registry/registry/schemagroups/io.intropy.maxbo.product/product-export.v1/2.json) uses: draft 2020-12, `title`, `description`, `type: object`, `additionalProperties: false`, `required[]`, `properties` with `type: string|integer|array`, `format: date-time`, `enum` of kebab-case strings, `items.$ref: "#/$defs/ExportEventFile"`, and a `$defs` map of nested object schemas. Its sibling `schema.yaml` documents: "Property names follow the System.Text.Json camelCase policy — first character lowercased only, so GTIN becomes gTIN — and nulls are omitted."

The generated types must land in the **shared-contracts** sibling project. Read /Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-templates/shared-contracts/ (template.yaml + skeleton) and /Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-templates/loader/template.yaml. **The user has decided the boundary: regenerable `.g.cs`.** Target tree:
```
Contracts/
  Generated/ProductExport.g.cs   <- do not edit; refreshed from the registry
  ProductExportRules.cs          <- hand-written partial
  Contracts.csproj
```

## What to design

1. **The generator package.** Where it lives, its exported API (input: schema document + root type name + namespace; output: file content(s)), and its internal model. It must be independently unit-testable with schema fixtures and no network.

2. **The type mapping**, as a decided table: object→record, array→IReadOnlyList<T>, $ref/$defs→named nested types, string/integer/number/boolean, `format` (date-time, date, uuid, …), nullable unions `["string","null"]`, enums of kebab strings, required vs optional. C# positional records require optional parameters last — say exactly how parameter order is made deterministic. **Note the hazard:** `json.Unmarshal` into a Go map loses `properties` declaration order; say how order is preserved.

3. **Unsupported constructs.** The institutional rule in this codebase is "borrow as much as reliably works; skip the rest, surface as Gaps" — never silently guess. content.content:
### Command verbs

One verb per meaning, used on every noun (`int`, `template`, `deploy`, ...).
The full set, grouped by what the verb does to the world:

**Read-only** — exit 0 even when the answer is "they disagree", never write
to git, never trigger a sync:

- **`list`** enumerates a collection: integrations on disk, templates in the
  library, published releases. It never prints one item's
  details.
- **`show`** prints the details of exactly one thing: a template's manifest,
  an integration's scaffold record. It never enumerates.
- **`status`** reports one component across every environment, one row
  each, and whether the rows agree. It never prints one environment's
  details — that is `show`.
- **`diff`** prints the rendered change a `sync` would apply, as the
  resources themselves. Both sides are committed revisions; it never diffs
  an uncommitted worktree.
- **`inspect`** prints the deployment model derived from one system topology:
  components, workloads, ports, and available local fixtures. It never
  renders manifests or writes project or Git state.
- **`render`** emits a complete Kubernetes YAML stream for one environment.
  It may ask for missing local fixture choices, buffers and validates the whole
  stream before writing stdout, writes all interaction and diagnostics to
  stderr, and never changes project, Git, or cluster state.

**Create or change project state** — may write files under the project.
Manifest creation may push a review branch, never the default branch:

- **`create`** makes something new from a template or from scaffolded
  parts: an integration, a system host, a release manifest to publish, or
  missing Kubernetes manifests on a GitOps review branch. Manifest creation
  accepts existing identical files but never replaces or deletes a file.
- **`add`** attaches something that already exists elsewhere to this
  project: a library registration. Unlike
  `create`, the content is pulled, not generated.
- **`update`** reconciles something installed against the ref its source
  now pins: a cached index against the registry. It never changes which
  ref is pinned — that is the publisher's job.
**Move or publish** — change what runs somewhere or what others can pull:

- **`publish`** pushes an immutable artifact to an OCI registry: a release
  manifest. What is published cannot be edited in
  place; a new version is a new publish.
- **`pin`** writes one component's image digest into one environment's
  overlay.
- **`promote`** copies the digests one environment runs into the next
  environment in the promotion graph.
- **`sync`** applies an environment's pending change through ArgoCD. It
  never decides what the change is — that is `pin` and `promote`.
- **`use`** selects which named customer context subsequent commands act
  on. Neither `update` (reconciles an installed thing against its source)
  nor `pin` (writes one component's digest) covers selecting the operator's
  active context, and `use` is the name kubeconfig muscle memory expects
  for it. It never creates or edits contexts — those are authored in the
  config file by hand.

Do not import kubectl's `get`/`describe` split — `int describe` was retired
because it described templates, not integrations. New verbs need a reason
that the set above cannot express, and the reason goes in this file with
the verb, not in a commit message.

---

## What this file is not

It does not replace `CONTRIBUTING.md` (workflow, tests, commit convention) or
`README.md` (what the CLI is). When those disagree with this file, this file
wins on writing style and loses on everything else.

# Extend scaffolding to consume the selected registry message

## Context

`feat/xregistry-message-subscriptions` shipped message *selection*: a template
parameter annotated `x-intropy-message-ref: true` holds an xRegistry message
id, and `int create` resolves it against one `GET /export` into `topic` +
`pubsub` values, a suggested `contract` name, and a `SubscriptionRecord` in
`.intropy/scaffold.json`. The CLI, the dashboard drawer and the interactive
prompt all offer the catalog.

What the message *carries* is still mostly unused, and in one place the
resolution has outrun the scaffold it feeds:

1. **The resolved pubsub never reaches the generated code.** Both
   `loader/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` and
   `extractor/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` hardcode
   `PubSubName = "pubsub"`, while `sys create`'s `Topics.cs.tmpl` correctly
   renders `TopicRef<T>.Define("{{ $t.pubsub }}", …)` from the record. Pick
   `io.intropy.maxbo.product.export` today and the host declares the topic on
   `product-distribution-pubsub` while the component subscribes on `pubsub`.
   The CloudEvents `type` and `source` reach no skeleton at all, so a loader
   accepts any event on its topic — even though the registry documents
   `source` as existing "for echo prevention".
2. **The payload schema is fetched and thrown away.**
   `xregistry.SchemaVersion.Document` already holds the inlined JSON Schema
   from `/export`; nothing reads it. Meanwhile `shared-contracts` renders
   `public record ProductExport();` and the scaffolded loader integration test
   carries a comment admitting it "deliberately uses its own field names
   instead of guessing the eventual shape".
3. **`subscriptions[]` is write-only.** No command or view reads it back, so
   the recorded message xid and schema version buy nothing yet — and the
   dashboard still ships a `PLACEHOLDER_SCHEMA` in `ContractDetail.tsx`
   because .NET hosts do not emit `contracts[].schema`.

Intended outcome: picking a message becomes the single act that wires a
subscriber — routing, envelope identity, and the payload type all follow from
it, and the record is readable enough afterwards to tell when the registry has
moved on.

*(Design in progress — sections below are being filled in.)*

# Extend scaffolding to consume the selected registry message

## Context

`feat/xregistry-message-subscriptions` shipped message *selection*: a template
parameter annotated `x-intropy-message-ref: true` holds an xRegistry message
id, and `int create` resolves it against one `GET /export` into `topic` +
`pubsub` values, a suggested `contract` name, and a `SubscriptionRecord` in
`.intropy/scaffold.json`. The CLI prompt, the dashboard drawer and
`int message list/show` all work.

What the message *carries* is still mostly unused, and in one place the
resolution has outrun the scaffold it feeds:

1. **The resolved pubsub never reaches the generated code.**
   `loader/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` and
   `extractor/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` hardcode
   `PubSubName = "pubsub"`, while `sys create`'s `Topics.cs.tmpl` correctly
   renders `TopicRef<T>.Define("{{ $t.pubsub }}", …)` from the record. Pick
   `io.intropy.maxbo.product.export` today and the host declares the topic on
   `product-distribution-pubsub` while the component subscribes on `pubsub`.
   The CloudEvents `type` and `source` reach no skeleton at all, so a loader
   accepts any event on its topic — though the registry documents `source` as
   existing "for echo prevention".
2. **The payload schema is fetched and thrown away.**
   `xregistry.SchemaVersion.Document` already holds the inlined JSON Schema;
   nothing reads it. Meanwhile `shared-contracts` renders
   `public record ProductExport();` and the scaffolded loader integration test
   admits in a comment that it "deliberately uses its own field names instead
   of guessing the eventual shape".
3. **`subscriptions[]` is write-only.** Nothing reads it back — not even
   `int show`, whose `formatScaffold` never prints it. The dashboard still
   ships a `PLACEHOLDER_SCHEMA` in `ContractDetail.tsx` because .NET hosts do
   not emit `contracts[].schema`.

Outcome: picking a message becomes the single act that wires a subscriber —
routing, envelope identity and the payload type all follow from it — and the
record stays readable enough afterwards to tell when the registry has moved on.

---

## Design decisions

**D1. The CLI flattens the schema; the template renders the C#.**
`internal/template/reserved.go` exists for exactly this case: *"spec.parameters
is scalar-only by design, so a skeleton cannot declare 'the list of ports' as a
parameter. These keys are how it gets one anyway: the caller injects the
structures after validation, and the skeleton ranges over them. Which files a
render produces is then decided by a spec.files condition over the same data."*
So a new reserved key carries a flattened field tree and the shared-contracts
skeleton ranges over it. All C# text stays in `intropy-templates`, versioned
with the template release; the CLI stays a schema flattener. Regeneration then
comes free — it is just a re-render, so `RenderUpdate` applies unchanged.

**D2. `spec.files` selects between the two shapes of the contract file.**
Today `{{ .contract }}.cs.tmpl` declares a primary constructor, and two records
cannot both do so. `FileRule{Path, When}` is matched against the *source* path
with sprig available (`internal/template/render.go:32`), so:

| source path | `when` |
|---|---|
| `Generated/{{ .contract }}.g.cs.tmpl` | shape present |
| `{{ .contract }}Rules.cs.tmpl` | shape present |
| `{{ .contract }}.cs.tmpl` | shape absent (today's sample/empty shell, untouched) |
| `OrderLine.cs.tmpl` | shape absent **and** `not .empty` (currently just the latter) |

The `.g.cs` holds `public partial record X(...)`; `XRules.cs` is the
parameterless `partial record X { }` companion for hand-written members.

**D3. The type mapping is CLI-owned and resolved in the flattener's output**,
so the template does no mapping. Decided table: object → nested record named
from its `$defs` key; array → `IReadOnlyList<T>`; string → `string` with
`format` date-time → `DateTimeOffset`, date → `DateOnly`, time → `TimeOnly`,
uuid → `Guid`, anything else → `string`; integer → `int` (`format: int64` →
`long`); number → `decimal`; boolean → `bool`; `["X","null"]` or absent from
`required` → `T?`. A string `enum` becomes `string` plus a
`static class <Prop>Values` of consts and an XML doc listing them — **not** a
C# enum: the registry's values are kebab-case (`product-attribute`), a real
enum needs a converter plus member-name mapping, and the schema is the
contract. `Contracts.csproj` is SDK-style with `Nullable` and `ImplicitUsings`
enabled, so `IReadOnlyList<>`/`DateTimeOffset` need no usings, nullable
annotations are meaningful, and `Generated/*.g.cs` is globbed in automatically.

**D4. Property order is preserved explicitly.** `json.Unmarshal` into a Go map
loses `properties` declaration order, and C# positional records require
optional parameters last. The flattener walks `properties` with a
`json.Decoder` token stream to keep order, then emits required members in
declaration order followed by optional ones in declaration order, each with
`= null`. Deterministic, and it compiles.

**D5. Unsupported constructs become Gaps, never guesses.** For `oneOf`,
`allOf`, `anyOf`, `patternProperties`, tuple-form `items`, a `$ref` outside
`#/$defs`, or recursion past a depth cap: the member's type becomes
`JsonElement`, the generated file carries a `// gap:` comment naming the
construct, and the flattener returns `[]Gap` that the create flow prints to
stderr. This is the house rule (borrow what reliably works, surface the rest as
Gaps) and it beats emitting a confidently wrong type.

**D6. The registry owns routing and envelope identity; the developer owns the
contract *name*.** `injectWiringValue` already encodes exactly this three-way
authority rule for `topic`/`pubsub` (identical accepted, conflicting `--set` an
error, any other layer yields with a stderr note). `eventType`/`eventSource`
join it. `contract` stays as it is — the registry supplies the *shape*, not the
type name.

**D7. `intropy int update` is the regeneration verb.** AGENTS.md:141 defines
`update` as *"reconciles something installed against the ref its source now
pins… It never changes which ref is pinned"*, and `int` has no `update` yet
(only create/describe/list/local/show). Which *message* a component subscribes
to is the developer's pin and stays untouched; the schema *version* is the
registry publisher's, so adopting it is reconciling, not re-pinning.
`RenderUpdate`'s `Baseline` is the shape re-flattened from the **recorded**
`SchemaVersion` — the export carries every version under `Schema.Versions`, so
the baseline is derivable — which makes an untouched `.g.cs` report `updated`
and a hand-edited one `conflict`. A recorded version the registry has since
dropped leaves `baselineKnown` false and everything differing conflicts, the
conservative fallback `render.go` already documents.

**D8. A reused shared-contracts project gets the generated subtree added.**
`internal/template/dependencies.go:97` skips a reused dependency entirely, so a
second component's contract would land nowhere. On reuse, when a shape is
present, render only the `Generated/**` and `<Contract>Rules.cs` rules through
`RenderUpdate` into the existing project.

---

## U1 — Resolved wiring reaches the generated code

Corrective; do this first, since everything else assumes the wiring is right.

**CLI**
- `internal/template/wiring.go` — add `KeyEventType = "eventType"`,
  `KeyEventSource = "eventSource"` to the vocabulary block.
- `internal/xregistry/client.go` — add `(*ResolvedMessage).CloudEventsSource()`
  beside the existing `CloudEventsType()`; both are two lines over
  `EnvelopeAttr.StringValue()`.
- `internal/template/messageref.go` `resolveMessageRef` — inject `eventType`
  and `eventSource` through the existing `injectWiringValue` so they inherit
  the D6 authority rule for free.
- `internal/xregistry/types.go` — model `Endpoint.EnvelopeOptions` /
  `ProtocolOptions` (currently unmodelled) and refuse a message whose envelope
  mode is not `structured`: the loader skeleton hand-parses structured
  CloudEvents JSON only, so a binary-mode message would scaffold a component
  that cannot read it.
- `internal/template/scaffold.go` — add `SchemaFingerprint` to
  `SubscriptionRecord` (hash of the schema document) so drift is exact even
  when a version is edited in place. Additive; no `ScaffoldSchemaVersion` bump,
  per the constant's own doc comment.
- `internal/system/assemble.go` — warn when the model holds two topics with the
  same `Name` but different `Pubsub`. That is precisely what a
  registry-resolved loader plus a hand-wired extractor produces today, and
  `byTopic` keys on `TopicKey` so the two never meet and nothing complains.

**Template library** (`intropy-templates`, branch `feat/loader-message-ref`)
- `loader/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` and
  `extractor/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` — `PubSubName = "{{ .pubsub }}"`.
- `loader/template.yaml` — add optional `eventType` and `eventSource`
  parameters, both `x-intropy-derived: true` (never prompted, still
  `--set`-able, per `missingRequired`'s skip).
- `loader/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` — emit `MessageType` and
  `ExpectedSource` when set.
- `loader/skeleton/src/Endpoints/LoaderEndpoints.cs.tmpl` — when `MessageType`
  is set, log-drop and ack SUCCESS on a delivery whose envelope `type` differs
  (a foreign type on a shared topic is not a retryable failure); when
  `ExpectedSource` is set, drop a self-published echo. Both gated so the manual
  path renders byte-identically to today.
- `extractor/template.yaml` — promote `pubsub` from a `spec.values` constant to
  a parameter defaulting to `pubsub`, so `internal/template/facts.go`'s
  existing `TopicKeys` prefill can carry a sibling loader's registry-resolved
  pubsub to the extractor.
- Both skeletons' `AGENTS.md.tmpl` / `README.md.tmpl` — `{{ .pubsub }}` in
  place of the literal `pubsub` in prose.

---

## U2 — `internal/contract`: JSON Schema → contract shape

New package, no network, no C# emission beyond type strings, fully
fixture-testable. Named for its domain like every sibling (`xregistry`,
`topology`, `system`).

```go
package contract

type Shape struct {
    Root  string  // Pascal-cased root type name
    Types []Type  // root first, then $defs in declaration order
}

type Type struct {
    Name, Title, Description string
    Members []Member  // required (declaration order), then optional
}

type Member struct {
    Name        string   // C# name: first character upper-cased only
    JSONName    string   // original property name
    CSType      string   // "string", "IReadOnlyList<ExportEventFile>", "DateTimeOffset?"
    Required    bool
    Description string
    EnumValues  []string // non-empty for a string enum
    Gap         string   // non-empty when the type could not be derived
}

type Gap struct{ Pointer, Construct string }

func FromSchema(doc []byte, root string) (Shape, []Gap, error)
```

`Name` inverts the documented serializer policy (`schema.yaml`: *"first
character lowercased only, so GTIN becomes gTIN"*), so `gTIN` → `GTIN` and
`exportId` → `ExportId` round-trip without a `[JsonPropertyName]`; emit one
only where the inverse is not exact.

**Tests** — the real
`~/dev/intropy/intropy-registry/registry/schemagroups/io.intropy.maxbo.product/product-export.v1/2.json`
as a fixture (nested `$defs`, a kebab enum, `format: date-time`, `required`,
`additionalProperties: false`), plus nullable unions, each D5 construct, and a
stability test that two runs produce identical output (D4's order guarantee).

---

## U3 — Generate into the shared-contracts project

- `internal/template/reserved.go` — add
  `ReservedContractShapeKey = "contractShape"`.
- `internal/template/messageref.go` — `ResolveSchema` already returns the
  `ResolvedSchema` whose `Version.Document` is the schema; flatten it with
  `contract.FromSchema` and hand the shape to the create flow alongside the
  `SubscriptionRecord`. Print gaps to `opts.Stderr`, the same channel the
  contract suggestion already notes on.
- `internal/template/dependencies.go` — inject the shape via `InjectReserved`
  for the shared-contracts dependency (after `Resolve`, per the function's own
  contract), and take the D8 reuse path.
- `intropy-templates/shared-contracts/template.yaml` — the four D2
  `spec.files` rules.
- `intropy-templates/shared-contracts/skeleton/Generated/{{ .contract }}.g.cs.tmpl`
  — ranges over `.contractShape`; header names the message xid, schema id and
  version and says do not edit.
- `intropy-templates/shared-contracts/skeleton/{{ .contract }}Rules.cs.tmpl` —
  the hand-written partial companion.
- Also delete `shared-contracts/skeleton/obj/**` — committed build artifacts
  that are currently rendered into every generated project.

---

## U4 — `intropy int update`

- `cmd/intropy/int_update.go` — mirror `cmd/intropy/sys_update.go`'s shape and
  flag plumbing; `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--registry-url`, `--output json`.
- `internal/template/update.go` — load the record via `FindScaffold`, fetch
  `/export` once, re-resolve each `SubscriptionRecord`, flatten the current
  default version (merged values) and the recorded version (baseline), then
  `RenderUpdate` the shared-contracts `Generated/**` subtree.
- Rewrite the record's `SchemaVersion` / `SchemaFingerprint` **last** and never
  on a conflict — `internal/system/update.go`'s discipline. Exit non-zero on an
  unforced conflict, naming the file.

---

## U5 — Read `subscriptions[]` back

- `cmd/intropy/int_show.go` `formatScaffold` — print a `Subscriptions:` block
  (there is none today). When a registry is configured, add one agreement line
  per subscription: message still present, channel unchanged, schema
  version/fingerprint unchanged. Exit 0 either way — the read-only verb group
  promises *"exit 0 even when the answer is 'they disagree'"*.
- `internal/dashboard` — serve the registry schema for a topic whose contract
  came from a subscription, joined `subscriptions[]` → `SchemaID` → export.
  `web/src/components/ContractDetail.tsx` prefers it over `PLACEHOLDER_SCHEMA`,
  feeding the existing `SchemaTree` (`FlowDetail.tsx:121`) untouched.
- `internal/dashboard/templates.go` `suggestForDir` — extend the per-message
  preview that already fills `FieldSpec.Wiring` with the message's schema, so
  the create drawer can show the payload shape at pick time through the same
  `SchemaTree`.

---

## Verification

**Go** — `go test ./...`; the new `internal/contract` fixture suite;
`messageref_test.go` extended for `eventType`/`eventSource` injection and the
shape hand-off; a `Create` test asserting the content of
`Contracts/Generated/ProductExport.g.cs`; an `int update` test covering all
four `FileOutcomeKind` values.

**Live, against the real registry** — `task dev:bg` in
`~/dev/intropy/intropy-registry`, then in a temp workspace:

1. `intropy int create loader --registry-url http://localhost:8787`, picking
   `io.intropy.maxbo.product.export`.
2. Assert `Constants.PubSubName == "product-distribution-pubsub"`,
   `Constants.MessageType == "io.intropy.maxbo.product.export"`, and that
   `Contracts/Generated/ProductExport.g.cs` carries
   `ExportId`/`Container`/`Files`/`StartedAt?` plus a nested
   `ExportEventFile` with its enum consts.
3. `intropy sys create`, then `dotnet build` and `task test` in the generated
   system — the real proof that the generated record satisfies the pipeline
   generics (`Loader<ProductExport, Out, Context>`) and that `Topics.cs` and
   `Constants.cs` now agree on the pubsub component.
4. Hand-edit the `.g.cs` and run `intropy int update` → `conflict`; revert →
   `unchanged`; bump the registry schema's default version → `updated`.
5. `intropy int show` → the subscription block plus agreement lines; then
   change the registry's channel and confirm it reports the disagreement at
   exit 0.
6. `intropy dashboard` — pick the message in the create drawer and confirm the
   schema tree renders; open the topic in the flow view and confirm the real
   schema has replaced the placeholder.

---

## Deliberately out of scope

- **Producer-side message refs.** The extractor keeps its heuristic
  `eventTypeValue` (`<org>.<first-topic-segment>.<last>`), which the registry's
  own README already flags as non-conforming. U1's `sys create` warning and the
  `pubsub` parameter promotion are the interim guard; making extractors declare
  what they publish is the natural next plan.
- **A real C# enum for schema enums** (D3).
- **A generated sample payload for the loader integration test.** Field *names*
  are derivable but values are not, and synthesizing them is the guessing this
  codebase avoids; the generated record at least makes the real names available
  to whoever fills the test in.
- Registry writes, and `envelopeoptions` beyond U1's structured-mode guard.

parameterless `partial record X { }` companion for hand-written members.

from its `$defs` key; array → `IReadOnlyList<T>`; string → `string` with
`format` date-time → `DateTimeOffset`, date → `DateOnly`, time → `TimeOnly`,
uuid → `Guid`, anything else → `string`; integer → `int` (`format: int64` →
`long`); number → `decimal`; boolean → `bool`; `["X","null"]` or absent from

`static class <Prop>Values` of consts and an XML doc listing them — **not** a

loses `properties` declaration order, and C# positional records require
optional parameters last. The flattener walks `properties` with a
`json.Decoder` token stream to keep order, then emits required members in
declaration order followed by optional ones in declaration order, each with
`= null`. Deterministic, and it compiles.

**D5. Unsupported constructs become Gaps, never guesses.** For `oneOf`,
`allOf`, `anyOf`, `patternProperties`, tuple-form `items`, a `$ref` outside
`#/$defs`, or recursion past a depth cap: the member's type becomes
`JsonElement`, the generated file carries a `// gap:` comment naming the
construct, and the flattener returns `[]Gap` that the create flow prints to
stderr. This is the house rule (borrow what reliably works, surface the rest as

**D6. The registry owns routing and envelope identity; the developer owns the
contract *name*.** `injectWiringValue` already encodes exactly this three-way
authority rule for `topic`/`pubsub` (identical accepted, conflicting `--set` an
error, any other layer yields with a stderr note). `eventType`/`eventSource`

type name.

**D7. `intropy int update` is the regeneration verb.** AGENTS.md:141 defines
`update` as *"reconciles something installed against the ref its source now
pins… It never changes which ref is pinned"*, and `int` has no `update` yet

registry publisher's, so adopting it is reconciling, not re-pinning.

dropped leaves `baselineKnown` false and everything differing conflicts, the

second component's contract would land nowhere. On reuse, when a shape is

+- `cmd/intropy/int_update.go` — mirror `cmd/intropy/sys_update.go`'s shape and
+  flag plumbing; `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--registry-url`, `--output json`.
+- `internal/template/update.go` — load the record via `FindScaffold`, fetch
+  `/export` once, re-resolve each `SubscriptionRecord`, flatten the current
+  default version (merged values) and the recorded version (baseline), then
+  `RenderUpdate` the shared-contracts `Generated/**` subtree.
+- Rewrite the record's `SchemaVersion` / `SchemaFingerprint` **last** and never
+  on a conflict — `internal/system/update.go`'s discipline. Exit non-zero on an
+  unforced conflict, naming the file.
+## U5 — Read `subscriptions[]` back
+- `cmd/intropy/int_show.go` `formatScaffold` — print a `Subscriptions:` block
+  (there is none today). When a registry is configured, add one agreement line
+  per subscription: message still present, channel unchanged, schema
+  version/fingerprint unchanged. Exit 0 either way — the read-only verb group
+  promises *"exit 0 even when the answer is 'they disagree'"*.

+  came from a subscription, joined `subscriptions[]` → `SchemaID` → export.
+  `web/src/components/ContractDetail.tsx` prefers it over `PLACEHOLDER_SCHEMA`,
+  feeding the existing `SchemaTree` (`FlowDetail.tsx:121`) untouched.

+  preview that already fills `FieldSpec.Wiring` with the message's schema, so
+  the create drawer can show the payload shape at pick time through the same
+  `SchemaTree`.

+**Go** — `go test ./...`; the new `internal/contract` fixture suite;
+`messageref_test.go` extended for `eventType`/`eventSource` injection and the
+shape hand-off; a `Create` test asserting the content of
+`Contracts/Generated/ProductExport.g.cs`; an `int update` test covering all
+four `FileOutcomeKind` values.
+**Live, against the real registry** — `task dev:bg` in
+`~/dev/intropy/intropy-registry`, then in a temp workspace:
+1. `intropy int create loader --registry-url http://localhost:8787`, picking
+   `io.intropy.maxbo.product.export`.
+2. Assert `Constants.PubSubName == "product-distribution-pubsub"`,
+   `Constants.MessageType == "io.intropy.maxbo.product.export"`, and that
+   `Contracts/Generated/ProductExport.g.cs` carries
+   `ExportId`/`Container`/`Files`/`StartedAt?` plus a nested
+   `ExportEventFile` with its enum consts.
+3. `intropy sys create`, then `dotnet build` and `task test` in the generated
+   system — the real proof that the generated record satisfies the pipeline
+   generics (`Loader<ProductExport, Out, Context>`) and that `Topics.cs` and
+   `Constants.cs` now agree on the pubsub component.
+4. Hand-edit the `.g.cs` and run `intropy int update` → `conflict`; revert →
+   `unchanged`; bump the registry schema's default version → `updated`.
+5. `intropy int show` → the subscription block plus agreement lines; then
+   change the registry's channel and confirm it reports the disagreement at
+   exit 0.
+6. `intropy dashboard` — pick the message in the create drawer and confirm the
+   schema tree renders; open the topic in the flow view and confirm the real
+   schema has replaced the placeholder.
+## Deliberately out of scope
+- **Producer-side message refs.** The extractor keeps its heuristic
+  `eventTypeValue` (`<org>.<first-topic-segment>.<last>`), which the registry's
+  own README already flags as non-conforming. U1's `sys create` warning and the
+  `pubsub` parameter promotion are the interim guard; making extractors declare
+  what they publish is the natural next plan.
+- **A real C# enum for schema enums** (D3).
+- **A generated sample payload for the loader integration test.** Field *names*
+  are derivable but values are not, and synthesizing them is the guessing this
+  codebase avoids; the generated record at least makes the real names available
+  to whoever fills the test in.

# Extend scaffolding to consume the selected registry message

## Context

`feat/xregistry-message-subscriptions` shipped message *selection*: a template
parameter annotated `x-intropy-message-ref: true` holds an xRegistry message
id, and `int create` resolves it against one `GET /export` into `topic` +
`pubsub` values, a suggested `contract` name, and a `SubscriptionRecord` in
`.intropy/scaffold.json`. The CLI prompt, the dashboard drawer and
`int message list/show` all work.

What the message *carries* is still mostly unused, and in one place the
resolution has outrun the scaffold it feeds:

1. **The resolved pubsub never reaches the generated code.**
   `loader/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` and
   `extractor/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` hardcode
   `PubSubName = "pubsub"`, while `sys create`'s `Topics.cs.tmpl` correctly
   renders `TopicRef<T>.Define("{{ $t.pubsub }}", …)` from the record. Pick
   `io.intropy.maxbo.product.export` today and the host declares the topic on
   `product-distribution-pubsub` while the component subscribes on `pubsub`.
   The CloudEvents `type` and `source` reach no skeleton at all, so a loader
   accepts any event on its topic — though the registry documents `source` as
   existing "for echo prevention".
2. **The payload schema is fetched and thrown away.**
   `xregistry.SchemaVersion.Document` already holds the inlined JSON Schema;
   nothing reads it. Meanwhile `shared-contracts` renders
   `public record ProductExport();` and the scaffolded loader integration test
   admits in a comment that it "deliberately uses its own field names instead
   of guessing the eventual shape".
3. **`subscriptions[]` is write-only.** Nothing reads it back — not even
   `int show`, whose `formatScaffold` never prints it. The dashboard still
   ships a `PLACEHOLDER_SCHEMA` in `ContractDetail.tsx` because .NET hosts do
   not emit `contracts[].schema`.

Outcome: picking a message becomes the single act that wires a subscriber —
routing, envelope identity and the payload type all follow from it — and the
record stays readable enough afterwards to tell when the registry has moved on.

---

## Design decisions

**D1. The CLI flattens the schema; the template renders the C#.**
`internal/template/reserved.go` exists for exactly this case: *"spec.parameters
is scalar-only by design, so a skeleton cannot declare 'the list of ports' as a
parameter. These keys are how it gets one anyway: the caller injects the
structures after validation, and the skeleton ranges over them. Which files a
render produces is then decided by a spec.files condition over the same data."*
So a new reserved key carries a flattened field tree and the shared-contracts
skeleton ranges over it. All C# text stays in `intropy-templates`, versioned
with the template release; the CLI stays a schema flattener. Regeneration then
comes free — it is just a re-render, so `RenderUpdate` applies unchanged.

**D2. `spec.files` selects between the two shapes of the contract file.**
Today `{{ .contract }}.cs.tmpl` declares a primary constructor, and two records
cannot both do so. `FileRule{Path, When}` is matched against the *source* path
with sprig available (`internal/template/render.go:32`), so:

| source path | `when` |
|---|---|
| `Generated/{{ .contract }}.g.cs.tmpl` | shape present |
| `{{ .contract }}Rules.cs.tmpl` | shape present |
| `{{ .contract }}.cs.tmpl` | shape absent (today's sample/empty shell, untouched) |
| `OrderLine.cs.tmpl` | shape absent **and** `not .empty` (currently just the latter) |

The `.g.cs` holds `public partial record X(...)`; `XRules.cs` is the
parameterless `partial record X { }` companion for hand-written members.

**D3. The type mapping is CLI-owned and resolved in the flattener's output**,
so the template does no mapping. Decided table: object → nested record named
from its `$defs` key; array → `IReadOnlyList<T>`; string → `string` with
`format` date-time → `DateTimeOffset`, date → `DateOnly`, time → `TimeOnly`,
uuid → `Guid`, anything else → `string`; integer → `int` (`format: int64` →
`long`); number → `decimal`; boolean → `bool`; `["X","null"]` or absent from
`required` → `T?`. A string `enum` becomes `string` plus a
`static class <Prop>Values` of consts and an XML doc listing them — **not** a
C# enum: the registry's values are kebab-case (`product-attribute`), a real
enum needs a converter plus member-name mapping, and the schema is the
contract. `Contracts.csproj` is SDK-style with `Nullable` and `ImplicitUsings`
enabled, so `IReadOnlyList<>`/`DateTimeOffset` need no usings, nullable
annotations are meaningful, and `Generated/*.g.cs` is globbed in automatically.

**D4. Property order is preserved explicitly.** `json.Unmarshal` into a Go map
loses `properties` declaration order, and C# positional records require
optional parameters last. The flattener walks `properties` with a
`json.Decoder` token stream to keep order, then emits required members in
declaration order followed by optional ones in declaration order, each with
`= null`. Deterministic, and it compiles.

**D5. Unsupported constructs become Gaps, never guesses.** For `oneOf`,
`allOf`, `anyOf`, `patternProperties`, tuple-form `items`, a `$ref` outside
`#/$defs`, or recursion past a depth cap: the member's type becomes
`JsonElement`, the generated file carries a `// gap:` comment naming the
construct, and the flattener returns `[]Gap` that the create flow prints to
stderr. This is the house rule (borrow what reliably works, surface the rest as
Gaps) and it beats emitting a confidently wrong type.

**D6. The registry owns routing and envelope identity; the developer owns the
contract *name*.** `injectWiringValue` already encodes exactly this three-way
authority rule for `topic`/`pubsub` (identical accepted, conflicting `--set` an
error, any other layer yields with a stderr note). `eventType`/`eventSource`
join it. `contract` stays as it is — the registry supplies the *shape*, not the
type name.

**D7. `intropy int update` is the regeneration verb.** AGENTS.md:141 defines
`update` as *"reconciles something installed against the ref its source now
pins… It never changes which ref is pinned"*, and `int` has no `update` yet
(only create/describe/list/local/show). Which *message* a component subscribes
to is the developer's pin and stays untouched; the schema *version* is the
registry publisher's, so adopting it is reconciling, not re-pinning.
`RenderUpdate`'s `Baseline` is the shape re-flattened from the **recorded**
`SchemaVersion` — the export carries every version under `Schema.Versions`, so
the baseline is derivable — which makes an untouched `.g.cs` report `updated`
and a hand-edited one `conflict`. A recorded version the registry has since
dropped leaves `baselineKnown` false and everything differing conflicts, the
conservative fallback `render.go` already documents.

**D8. A reused shared-contracts project gets the generated subtree added.**
`internal/template/dependencies.go:97` skips a reused dependency entirely, so a
second component's contract would land nowhere. On reuse, when a shape is
present, render only the `Generated/**` and `<Contract>Rules.cs` rules through
`RenderUpdate` into the existing project.

---

## U1 — Resolved wiring reaches the generated code

Corrective; do this first, since everything else assumes the wiring is right.

**CLI**
- `internal/template/wiring.go` — add `KeyEventType = "eventType"`,
  `KeyEventSource = "eventSource"` to the vocabulary block.
- `internal/xregistry/client.go` — add `(*ResolvedMessage).CloudEventsSource()`
  beside the existing `CloudEventsType()`; both are two lines over
  `EnvelopeAttr.StringValue()`.
- `internal/template/messageref.go` `resolveMessageRef` — inject `eventType`
  and `eventSource` through the existing `injectWiringValue` so they inherit
  the D6 authority rule for free.
- `internal/xregistry/types.go` — model `Endpoint.EnvelopeOptions` /
  `ProtocolOptions` (currently unmodelled) and refuse a message whose envelope
  mode is not `structured`: the loader skeleton hand-parses structured
  CloudEvents JSON only, so a binary-mode message would scaffold a component
  that cannot read it.
- `internal/template/scaffold.go` — add `SchemaFingerprint` to
  `SubscriptionRecord` (hash of the schema document) so drift is exact even
  when a version is edited in place. Additive; no `ScaffoldSchemaVersion` bump,
  per the constant's own doc comment.
- `internal/system/assemble.go` — warn when the model holds two topics with the
  same `Name` but different `Pubsub`. That is precisely what a
  registry-resolved loader plus a hand-wired extractor produces today, and
  `byTopic` keys on `TopicKey` so the two never meet and nothing complains.

**Template library** (`intropy-templates`, branch `feat/loader-message-ref`)
- `loader/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` and
  `extractor/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` — `PubSubName = "{{ .pubsub }}"`.
- `loader/template.yaml` — add optional `eventType` and `eventSource`
  parameters, both `x-intropy-derived: true` (never prompted, still
  `--set`-able, per `missingRequired`'s skip).
- `loader/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` — emit `MessageType` and
  `ExpectedSource` when set.
- `loader/skeleton/src/Endpoints/LoaderEndpoints.cs.tmpl` — when `MessageType`
  is set, log-drop and ack SUCCESS on a delivery whose envelope `type` differs
  (a foreign type on a shared topic is not a retryable failure); when
  `ExpectedSource` is set, drop a self-published echo. Both gated so the manual
  path renders byte-identically to today.
- `extractor/template.yaml` — promote `pubsub` from a `spec.values` constant to
  a parameter defaulting to `pubsub`, so `internal/template/facts.go`'s
  existing `TopicKeys` prefill can carry a sibling loader's registry-resolved
  pubsub to the extractor.
- Both skeletons' `AGENTS.md.tmpl` / `README.md.tmpl` — `{{ .pubsub }}` in
  place of the literal `pubsub` in prose.

---

## U2 — `internal/contract`: JSON Schema → contract shape

New package, no network, no C# emission beyond type strings, fully
fixture-testable. Named for its domain like every sibling (`xregistry`,
`topology`, `system`).

```go
package contract

type Shape struct {
    Root  string  // Pascal-cased root type name
    Types []Type  // root first, then $defs in declaration order
}

type Type struct {
    Name, Title, Description string
    Members []Member  // required (declaration order), then optional
}

type Member struct {
    Name        string   // C# name: first character upper-cased only
    JSONName    string   // original property name
    CSType      string   // "string", "IReadOnlyList<ExportEventFile>", "DateTimeOffset?"
    Required    bool
    Description string
    EnumValues  []string // non-empty for a string enum
    Gap         string   // non-empty when the type could not be derived
}

type Gap struct{ Pointer, Construct string }

func FromSchema(doc []byte, root string) (Shape, []Gap, error)
```

`Name` inverts the documented serializer policy (`schema.yaml`: *"first
character lowercased only, so GTIN becomes gTIN"*), so `gTIN` → `GTIN` and
`exportId` → `ExportId` round-trip without a `[JsonPropertyName]`; emit one
only where the inverse is not exact.
