# JSON Schema → C# record generation

## 0. What the code actually allows (the constraints that drove every decision)

Five findings from reading fix most of the design space:

1. **`cmd/intropy/helptext_test.go:70-108` is a hard gate on the command surface.** It enumerates the AGENTS.md verb set and fails any command whose leaf name is outside it. `generate` is not in the set; `update` is. A `contract` noun would also need adding to the `notVerbs` map. This makes `int update` not a preference but the only surface that ships without amending AGENTS.md first.
2. **`internal/template/dependencies.go:88-93` skips an existing dependency entirely** — no render, no values applied, `Action: "exists"`. So anything that must land in the shared project on a *second* component's create cannot come from the shared-contracts skeleton. That decides question 5 on its own.
3. **`FileRule.Path` is matched raw against the source path** (`internal/template/filter.go:60-73`, `matchSkeletonPath` → `path.Match`, never rendered). It cannot cross `/`. So a rule for `skeleton/{{ .contract }}.cs.tmpl` must be a glob (`*.cs.tmpl`), and grouping the sample files into a subdirectory is impossible because `renderPath` derives the destination from the whole relative source path.
4. **`internal/template/manifest.go:135-160` (`extractPropertyOrder`) is the in-repo precedent for exactly the ordering hazard.** `Spec.UnmarshalYAML` decodes into a map *and* walks the `yaml.Node` to capture `properties` declaration order, because "Go maps don't preserve YAML order". The generator repeats that shape for JSON.
5. **`RenderUpdate` (`internal/template/render.go:112-207`) cannot be called** — it walks a `srcDir` of skeleton files, and the `.g.cs` has no skeleton file. But its *classification rule* and its `FileOutcome` types transfer exactly, including the "baseline render that fails is unknown, not an error" fallback at lines 178-187.

---

## 1. The generator package

**`internal/csharpgen/`** — new package. Name follows the repo's "the domain thing" convention (`internal/xregistry`, `internal/kustomize`, `internal/topology`) and keeps the language in the name so a future TypeScript target is a sibling, not a rewrite. It is pure: no filesystem, no network, no clock, no `os`, and it does not import `internal/template` (which is what lets `internal/template` orchestrate it without a cycle).

Files:
- `internal/csharpgen/doc.go` — package doc: what it consumes, what it refuses, and why the output is a pure function of its input.
- `internal/csharpgen/schema.go` — the ordered JSON Schema model + `UnmarshalJSON`.
- `internal/csharpgen/plan.go` — schema model → C# type plan (naming, mapping, gaps).
- `internal/csharpgen/emit.go` — plan → source text.
- `internal/csharpgen/sample.go` — plan → minimal schema-valid JSON payload.
- `internal/csharpgen/{schema,plan,emit,sample}_test.go`
- `internal/csharpgen/testdata/` — input `*.json`, expected `*.g.cs`, expected `*.sample.json`.

`testdata/` is a deviation: there are no `testdata` directories anywhere in this repo today (verified). Justified because the load-bearing fixture is the real 2.4 KB `product-export.v1/2.json`, and as a Go raw string literal it is unreadable and un-diffable. No `-update` flag — the golden files are hand-maintained, which is only tolerable because of the no-timestamp decision in §1.3.

### 1.1 Exported API

```go
// Options is the whole input. There is no filesystem, network, or clock
// behind Generate: the same Options always produce the same bytes, which is
// what makes an "unchanged" verdict on a regenerated file meaningful.
type Options struct {
    // Document is the inlined JSON Schema document — xregistry
    // SchemaVersion.Document verbatim.
    Document json.RawMessage
    // RootName is the C# name for the root record, PascalCase. It is the
    // resolved contract value, not derived here: the developer may always
    // override it, and a generator that re-derived it could disagree.
    RootName string
    // Namespace is the file-scoped namespace, the shared-contracts project
    // name ("Contracts"). Emitted verbatim, never derived from the folder.
    Namespace string
    // Header is the provenance the file states about itself.
    Header Header
}

// Header is the provenance block. It deliberately carries no timestamp and
// no tool version: the bytes must be a pure function of the schema, or a
// CLI upgrade would rewrite every generated file and a hand edit would be
// indistinguishable from churn.
type Header struct {
    Message        string // message xid
    Schema         string // schema xid
    SchemaVersion  string // schema version id
    RefreshCommand string // the exact command that rewrites this file
}

// Gap is one shape-bearing construct the generator declined to map.
type Gap struct {
    Pointer   string // JSON pointer into the document
    Construct string // "oneOf", "patternProperties", "prefixItems", ...
    Detail    string // one lowercase sentence, house voice
}

// Result is the generated file plus everything a caller must report.
type Result struct {
    Source   string   // complete file content, LF, 4-space indent, trailing newline
    RootType string
    Types    []string // every emitted type, root first, nested as "Root.Nested"
    Gaps     []Gap
    Notes    []string // value-only constructs observed (enum values, pattern, if/then)
}

// Generate compiles the document into one C# source file. A construct that
// changes the payload's shape and cannot be mapped becomes a Gap on the
// member carrying it, so the rest of the record still lands; a document
// whose root cannot be a record at all is an UnsupportedRootError, so a
// caller leaves the hand-written shell in place rather than write a file
// that does not compile.
func Generate(opts Options) (*Result, error)

// SampleOptions and Sample produce the minimal schema-valid payload for
// the same document: required members only, deterministic literals.
type SampleOptions struct{ Document json.RawMessage }

// Sample returns the payload and whether it is schema-valid. A document
// whose required members cannot be filled without guessing — a required
// string constrained by an arbitrary pattern, or a required member that is
// a Gap — yields ok=false and a reason, never an invented value.
func Sample(opts SampleOptions) (payload []byte, reason string, ok bool)

// UnsupportedRootError reports a document whose root cannot become a record.
type UnsupportedRootError struct{ Reason string }
func (e *UnsupportedRootError) Error() string
```

### 1.2 Internal model and the ordering hazard

`json.Unmarshal` into `map[string]any` loses `properties` order. Fix, mirroring `extractPropertyOrder`:

```go
type node struct {
    Raw json.RawMessage

    Title, Description string
    Types  []string        // normalized: "type" as string or []string
    Format string
    Ref    string
    Enum   []json.RawMessage
    Const  json.RawMessage

    Properties []named     // ordered slice, not a map
    Required   []string
    Defs       []named     // ordered slice
    Items      *node
    PrefixItems []*node
    AdditionalProperties *node
    AdditionalPropertiesFalse bool
    OneOf, AnyOf, AllOf []*node

    HasPatternProperties bool
    ValueOnly []string     // minimum, maxLength, pattern, if/then/else, not, ...
}
type named struct{ Name string; Node *node }

func (n *node) UnmarshalJSON(b []byte) error // json.Decoder token walk
```

`UnmarshalJSON` drives a `json.Decoder` over its own bytes and reads key/value pairs in stream order, so `properties` and `$defs` keep declaration order. Stdlib only — no new module dependency.

**Parameter order is decided as:** required properties in `properties` declaration order, then optional properties in `properties` declaration order. Two consequences stated explicitly:
- The `required` **array's** order is never used. It is an arbitrary authoring artifact; `properties` order is how a human reads the document. Same reasoning as `extractPropertyOrder` preferring YAML declaration order over the map.
- Because C# requires optional parameters last, adding a new *required* property mid-document shifts positional arguments. This is source-breaking for positional construction and must be in the generated file's header. It is **not** wire-breaking: System.Text.Json binds constructor parameters by name, so serialization is order-independent.

---

## 2. The type mapping (decided table)

Naming rule first, because it makes the rest safe. `schema.yaml` documents that the wire names came out of `JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase` — "first character lowercased only, so GTIN becomes gTIN". The exact inverse is: **uppercase the first character, change nothing else.** `exportId` → `ExportId`, `gTIN` → `GTIN`. No kebab/snake splitting, no acronym heuristics.

And: **every parameter carries `[property: JsonPropertyName("<exact json name>")]`.** This is what makes identifier mangling lossless — the wire contract lives in the attribute, so the C# identifier is free — and it makes the record correct regardless of the host's `JsonSerializerOptions`. The loader's `Deserializer.cs.tmpl` currently relies on `PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true`; the generated record must not depend on that.

| JSON Schema | C# | Note |
|---|---|---|
| root `type: object` + `properties` | `public partial record <RootName>(...)` | `partial`, primary constructor here |
| `$defs` object schema (reachable) | nested `public partial record <Def>(...)` | inside the root record |
| `$ref: "#/$defs/X"` | `<RootName>.X` | resolved to a *name*, never inlined |
| `$ref: "#"` | `<RootName>` | root self-reference |
| inline `type: object` + `properties` | nested record named from the property path (`properties.address` → `Address`; `properties.files.items` → `FilesItem`) | no singularization — that would be a guess |
| `type: array` + `items: S` | `IReadOnlyList<map(S)>` | matches the existing `OrderLine` sample |
| `type: string` | `string` | |
| `string` + `format: date-time` | `DateTimeOffset` | |
| `string` + `format: date` / `time` / `duration` | `DateOnly` / `TimeOnly` / `TimeSpan` | |
| `string` + `format: uuid` | `Guid` | |
| `string` + `format: uri`/`uri-reference`/`byte` | `string` | deliberately **not** `Uri`/`byte[]`: those throw on a malformed producer value, turning a business problem into a redelivery loop |
| `string` + unknown `format` | `string` | format recorded in the doc comment |
| `type: integer` (no format, or `int64`) | `long` | JSON integers are unbounded |
| `integer` + `format: int32` | `int` | |
| `type: number` | `decimal` | matches the hand-written `decimal UnitPrice` sample; integration money semantics |
| `number` + `format: float`/`double` | `float`/`double` | |
| `type: boolean` | `bool` | |
| `enum` of strings | `string` + allowed values in the `///` doc comment | see below |
| `const` | the const's JSON kind + value in the doc comment | |
| `type: ["T","null"]` | `map(T)?` | nullability, independent of optionality |
| `anyOf`/`oneOf` of exactly `[S, {"type":"null"}]` | `map(S)?` | the nullable idiom is reliable |
| `allOf` of exactly one `$ref` | that `$ref`'s type | reliable |
| `type` absent / `{}` / `true` | `JsonElement` | |
| `additionalProperties: S`, no `properties` | `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, map(S)>` | |

**Required vs optional:**

| | emitted |
|---|---|
| required, non-nullable | `T Name` — leading group, no default |
| required, nullable union | `T? Name` — leading group, no default |
| optional (any type) | `T? Name = null` — trailing group |

Optional is **always** nullable with `= null`, including value types (`long?`, `bool?`, `IReadOnlyList<T>?`). This is load-bearing: whether System.Text.Json honors a C# default parameter value or passes `default(T)` for an absent JSON property, the result is `null` either way. A non-nullable `long Count = 0` would silently read a missing property as `0`.

**Enums map to `string`, not to a C# `enum`.** Rationale: the registry's own `schema.yaml` declares `compatibility: backward`, so a producer may add an enum member. A strongly-typed enum throws on an unlisted value, which in the loader pipeline is a *technical* failure → `DeliveryAck.Retry` → an infinite redelivery loop on a message the Validator would have routed as a business incident. A `string` lets the value reach the Validator, which is where the business decision belongs. The allowed values go in the `///` doc comment and into `Result.Notes`. A future opt-in (`--enums=strong`, emitting `[JsonStringEnumMemberName("product-attribute")]`, .NET 9+) is noted but not built.

**Nested types are nested, not top-level.** `$defs` types become nested records inside the root record, referenced as `<RootName>.<Def>` (emitted fully qualified in the parameter list, so C# name lookup in a primary constructor parameter list is not load-bearing). Rationale: it makes each `.g.cs` hermetic, which is exactly what makes "delete and regenerate" safe and what lets two components' contracts coexist in one `Contracts` project without a cross-schema name registry. `$defs` are document-local by definition; a document-local C# type mirrors that. Cost — verbose use sites — is accepted and stated in the file header. Nested records are also `partial`, so the hand-written file can extend them.

**Recursion falls out for free** because `$ref` resolves to a *type name* and is never structurally inlined. `record Node(IReadOnlyList<Node>? Children = null)` is legal C#. The traversal needs a visited set only to avoid re-planning a def, not to break an infinite expansion.

Identifier safety, in order: PascalCase the first character → strip characters illegal in a C# identifier and PascalCase across the removed boundaries → prefix `@` if the result is a C# keyword → suffix `Value` if it collides with the enclosing type name or a record-synthesized member (`Equals`, `GetHashCode`, `ToString`, `Deconstruct`, `PrintMembers`, `EqualityContract`). If two distinct JSON names collapse to one identifier, or an identifier comes out empty, that is a **type-level refusal** — an ambiguous mapping is the one case mangling cannot fix.

Only `$defs` **reachable** from the root are emitted. An unreachable def is dead schema; emitting it invites a collision and is not part of the payload's shape. Unreachable defs go into `Notes`.

No `[JsonExtensionData]` member is ever emitted, for `additionalProperties: false` or otherwise — that would be inventing a member.

---

## 3. Unsupported constructs

The rule is split by **what the construct affects**, which is the distinction that makes the policy predictable:

**Shape-bearing and unmappable → member-level gap.** The property is still emitted, as `JsonElement?` in the trailing optional group, with a `///` doc comment naming the construct. Nothing is lost (the raw JSON stays reachable), nothing is guessed, and the record remains complete against the schema — the developer projects it into a real shape in the hand-written partial, which is precisely what the partial split is for. This is "borrow as much as reliably works" applied per property.

- `oneOf` / `anyOf` / `allOf` beyond the two reliable idioms in §2
- `patternProperties`
- `prefixItems` / tuple-form `items: [S1, S2]` — no STJ-bindable C# shape
- `$ref` that is external (`http://…`, another file) or points anywhere other than `#/$defs/*` or `#`
- an inline nested-object name that collides with a `$defs`-derived name

**Value-only → informational note, never a gap.** These do not change the shape, so a gap would be a false alarm: `not`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `dependentSchemas`, `dependentRequired`, `minimum`/`maximum`/`multipleOf`, `minLength`/`maxLength`/`pattern`, `minItems`/`maxItems`/`uniqueItems`, `additionalProperties: false`, `$comment`, `readOnly`/`writeOnly`, an unrecognized `$schema` draft. They land in `Result.Notes` and, where they describe one property, in that property's doc comment.

**Root cannot be a record → `UnsupportedRootError`, nothing written.** The hand-written shell stays and the create still succeeds:
- root is not `type: object` (a top-level array or scalar payload)
- root `type: object` with no `properties`
- root-level `oneOf`/`anyOf` selecting between shapes (a polymorphic payload needs a discriminator design)
- two JSON property names collapsing to one C# identifier

**Surfacing — all three channels, each for a different reader:**

1. **In the generated file**, a header block with the provenance, the refresh command, and a `Gaps:` list; plus a `///` comment on each gap member. The file is what the developer opens; a gap invisible there is a gap nobody acts on.
2. **On stderr**, one lowercase line per gap at create/update time, per AGENTS.md ("stderr is for everything else").
3. **In the machine-readable result** — `CreateResult.Contracts[].Gaps` and `int update --output json` — because the agent and shaping workflows consume `CreateResult`, and a gap is only actionable to them as data.
4. **In `.intropy/scaffold.json`**, on the subscription record (§5), so drift detection has a baseline.

Never a refusal of the create. A gap is information, not a failure.

---

## 4. The partial-record split

Today `shared-contracts/skeleton/{{ .contract }}.cs.tmpl` emits either `public record ProductExport();` or the `Order` sample — both with a primary constructor, which collides with the `.g.cs` part.

**Mechanism: a `spec.files` `When` gate on shared-contracts, driven by a value the parent forwards.** This is the right mechanism, for three reasons visible in the code: `spec.files` conditions are evaluated against the dependency's *own* resolved values inside `renderDependency` → `renderCreateOutput` → `RenderFiltered(…, tmpl.Spec.Files)`, so the gate is in scope; `manifest.go:validate` compiles every `When` at load time so an authoring error surfaces before anything is written; and `filter.go`'s documented "first matching rule decides, a path no rule matches is included" keeps every other skeleton file untouched.

`intropy-templates/shared-contracts/template.yaml`:

```yaml
      generated:
        type: boolean
        title: Generated contracts
        description: When true, the contract records are generated from the registry's JSON Schema into Generated/*.g.cs by the CLI, and no sample contract shell is scaffolded — two records cannot both declare a primary constructor.
        default: false
  files:
    # A generated contract's primary constructor lives in
    # Generated/<contract>.g.cs; a scaffolded shell would declare a second
    # one for the same record.
    - path: "*.cs.tmpl"
      when: "{{ not .generated }}"
```

One rule, one glob. `*.cs.tmpl` cannot cross `/`, so it matches exactly `{{ .contract }}.cs.tmpl` and `OrderLine.cs.tmpl` and nothing under the (regrettably committed) `obj/` tree. It also cleans up a current wart: with `empty: true`, `OrderLine.cs.tmpl` renders an empty `OrderLine.cs` today.

The `.gitignore` is **not** changed: `Generated/*.g.cs` is committed. Offline and registry-less CI builds, and a reviewable diff when a schema version moves, are both worth more than a clean tree. Optionally add `*.g.cs linguist-generated=true` to a `.gitattributes` so GitHub collapses it by default while keeping the diff available — not `-diff`, which would hide the review we want.

`README.md.tmpl` and `AGENTS.md.tmpl` in shared-contracts gain `{{- if .generated }}` branches: the "Important files" list must name `Generated/<contract>.g.cs` as machine-owned and never hand-edited, and `<contract>Rules.cs` as the hand-written half.

The `<Contract>Rules.cs` stub is **written by the CLI, not the skeleton** — see §5.

The parent side, on `loader/template.yaml` (and `extractor/template.yaml` when it gains a message-ref parameter; `transactional` has neither a message-ref nor a shared-contracts dependency, verified):

```yaml
      contractGenerated:
        type: boolean
        title: Generated contract
        description: Whether the contract records come from the message's registry schema. Filled by the CLI when a subscription resolves to a schema it can compile; never set by hand.
        default: false
        x-intropy-derived: true
```
```yaml
  dependencies:
    - template: shared-contracts
      output: '{{ .contracts }}'
      values:
        name: '{{ .contracts }}'
        contract: '{{ .contract }}'
        empty: '{{ .empty }}'
        generated: '{{ .contractGenerated }}'
```

Declared rather than smuggled in as an undeclared key, for consistency with how `topic` and `contract` were done: `x-intropy-derived` exists precisely so a CLI-authored parameter is visible to `template show`, skipped by `missingRequired` (`values.go:389-398`), hidden by the dashboard form, and still overridable with `--set`. Declaring it also means `renderDependencyValues`' `missingkey=error` template can reference it unconditionally, and shared-contracts' `Resolve` coerces the rendered `"true"` to a `bool` via `coerceKnownFieldValue` against the declared `type: boolean`.

## 5. Who writes the `.g.cs`

**The CLI writes it, after `processDependencies`.** Passing generated source through a template value is rejected on four counts, three of them structural:

1. `dependencies.go:88-93` skips an existing dependency entirely, so a second component reusing the `Contracts` project would never get its `.g.cs` — the case that matters most.

### The shared project already exists

`processDependencies` returns `Action: "exists"` and renders nothing. Two sub-cases:

**Same contract name, existing project scaffolded with `generated: false`.** A hand-scaffolded `<Contract>.cs` with a primary constructor is on disk and would collide. **Refuse by default**, report it as a conflict, and name the remediation:

```
Contracts/ProductExport.cs declares a primary constructor for the same record as Generated/ProductExport.g.cs
delete Contracts/ProductExport.cs and re-run, or re-run with --force to remove it
```

Detected from the dependency's own scaffold record (`values.generated != true`, `values.contract == <thisContract>`) plus the file's presence. `--force` removes it **only when its bytes equal a re-render of the shell from that record's own values** — the same baseline idea as `RenderUpdate`. A shell the developer edited is never removed, even with `--force`. The default refusal is not timidity: `renderDependency` already documents why `--force` does not propagate to a dependency — "overwriting a shared project that other components already reference is destructive at a distance" — and deleting a type from it is strictly worse.

**Different contract name.** No collision. Write `Generated/<NewContract>.g.cs` and, create-only, `<NewContract>Rules.cs`. Because both are CLI-written, the reuse path behaves identically to the first-component path — the asymmetry that a skeleton-owned stub would have introduced does not exist.

### Two components, one project

Two distinct contracts → two `Generated/*.g.cs` files, each hermetic. Cross-schema `$defs` collisions (both schemas defining `Address`) cannot occur, because nested types are nested (§2). The same contract name from two different schema xids **is** a real conflict: the second component would regenerate the first's file from a different schema. Detected because the file exists and matches neither the merged nor the baseline render → `OutcomeConflict`, refused with both message xids named. No `--force` shortcut here; the two components genuinely disagree about what `ProductExport` is.

`.csproj` needs no change — `Microsoft.NET.Sdk` globs `**/*.cs`, so `Generated/` compiles automatically.


Generation runs **before any file is written**, inside `prepareCreateTemplate`, and that is the point: the decision to suppress the skeleton shell and the decision that a generated record exists are the same decision, taken from the same in-memory result. ## 6. Regeneration

**Surface: `intropy int update [dir]`.** `cmd/intropy/int_update.go` does not exist today (verified). Rationale, in priority order: `helptext_test.go:70-108` accepts `update` and rejects `generate`; AGENTS.md's `update` — "reconciles something installed against the ref its source now pins… It never changes which ref is pinned — that is the publisher's job" — describes this operation exactly, since the *registry* is the publisher and its `isdefault` flag is the pin; and `int` is where a per-integration operation belongs, whereas a `contract` noun would be a fifth place to look for a property of one integration.

```
intropy int update [dir]

Short: Reconcile an integration's generated contracts against the registry
Long:  Regenerate the contract records an integration's registry subscriptions
       resolve to, from the schema version the registry now flags default.
       Reads .intropy/scaffold.json for the subscription and the sibling
       contracts project; writes Generated/<contract>.g.cs there and the
       integration test's sample payload. A file identical to what the update
       would write is kept, a missing one is written, one matching what the
       recorded schema version generated is updated, and a hand-edited one is
       an error unless --force. It does not re-render the integration's
       skeleton and does not change the template pin.

Flags: --dry-run, --force, --output (flagUsageOutputJSONOnly),
       --registry-url (flagUsageRegistryURL), --schema-version
```

`--schema-version` pins an explicit version instead of the registry default — the *user* pinning, not the command choosing, exactly as `sys update --template-version` does.

**Reuse `RenderUpdate`'s machinery? Its types and its rule, yes; its walker, no.** `RenderUpdate` walks a `srcDir` of skeleton files and there is no skeleton file for a `.g.cs`. But the classification maps one-to-one:

| `RenderUpdate` | contract regeneration |
|---|---|
| merged render (current values) | `Generate` with the **current** schema version's document |
| baseline render (recorded values) | `Generate` with the **recorded** `SubscriptionRecord.SchemaVersion` document |
| absent → `created` | same |
| == merged → `unchanged` | same |
| == baseline → `updated` | same — the developer never touched it, safe to overwrite |
| else → `conflict` (or `updated` with `--force`) | same — a hand-edited `.g.cs` reports a conflict, is not clobbered |

So: **factor the switch out** of `RenderUpdate` (`render.go:188-199`) into

```go
// ClassifyUpdate decides one destination file's outcome from what an update
// would write, what the baseline would have written, and what is on disk.
// An unknown baseline falls back to the strict rule: every differing file
// conflicts.
func ClassifyUpdate(existing, merged, baseline []byte, existed, baselineKnown, force bool) FileOutcomeKind
```

and have both callers use it. `render_test.go` already covers the four outcomes, so the refactor is verified by tests that exist; and it stops the two paths from drifting on the one rule that protects a developer's edits.

Because `/export` inlines every schema version, the recorded version's document is normally still available (`Schema.Versions[recordedID]`). When it is not, the baseline is **unknown**, and the strict rule applies — the exact fallback `RenderUpdate` already documents at `render.go:178-187` ("A baseline render that fails … is unknown, not an error: the strict comparison below then decides, conservatively"). That symmetry is the reason to state the whole thing this way.

**Why the header carries no timestamp and no tool version:** either would make every file classify as `updated` on the next run (or after any CLI upgrade), permanently destroying the `unchanged` verdict and hiding real hand edits inside manufactured churn. Generator-version drift is instead detected honestly — the regenerated bytes differ, which is a real diff a human reads.

**Record last, never on a conflict.** The scaffold record's `SchemaVersion` and `Generated` are rewritten only after every file landed with no conflicts, so a failed update retries against an honest baseline. Lifted verbatim from `system/update.go:180-190`.

Other cases `int update` must handle:
- recorded message xid no longer in the registry → error naming the xid plus `use 'intropy message list' to see the messages in the registry` (reuse `resolveMessage`'s wrapper in `cmd/intropy/message.go`).
- the developer changed `contract`, so the old `.g.cs` filename is orphaned → stderr note naming the file; **never deleted**, because the CLI must not remove a `.cs` it cannot prove it wrote. `--force` removes it when its bytes match the baseline generation.
- no subscriptions in the record → `no registry subscriptions found` on stderr, exit 0. Empty state, house voice, no period.
- a `.g.cs` whose gaps changed but whose bytes did not → nothing to do; the gaps are already in the file.

Out of scope, and the `Long` must say so: re-rendering the component skeleton at a newer template version. Naming it keeps a future author from assuming `int update` already promised it.

`README.md` needs an `### Update an integration` subsection under `## Integrations (intropy int)` and a row in `## Command overview`.

## 7. Test fixture generation

**Yes — generate a sample payload, as data, not as code.**

The scaffolded `DeliveryIntegrationTests.cs.tmpl` comment ("this file deliberately uses its own field names instead of guessing the eventual shape") is *true today and false the moment a schema is known*. Worse, its `ValidRecordJson` will not deserialize into the generated record, so the first test the developer fixes after implementing `Deserializer` fails for a reason that has nothing to do with their code.

Generating test data is not the forbidden guess. The forbidden guess is about the *contract*; a sample payload is about *values*, it is derived deterministically, and — decisively — **it is mechanically checkable**: `github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v5` is already in `go.mod` (used only by `internal/template/values.go` today) and validates the sample against its own schema before it is written. If it does not validate, it is not written, and that is a stderr note, not an error. That turns "never silently guess" from a convention into an enforced property.

Path: `<component>/test/<Name>.Test.Integration/Payloads/<Contract>.sample.g.json`. In the component's tree, not the contracts library — a contracts library must not ship test fixtures. Same `.g.` marker, same three-way classification, so a developer who edits it gets a conflict rather than losing it.

Template change (loader, and extractor once it gains a message-ref), gated on `{{ if .contractGenerated }}`:

```csharp
// Sample payload generated from the message's registry schema; refreshed by
// `intropy int update`. It carries the schema's required members only.
private static readonly string ValidRecordJson =
    File.ReadAllText(Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, "Payloads", "{{ .contract }}.sample.g.json"));
```

plus, in `{{ .name }}.Test.Integration.csproj.tmpl`:

```xml
<None Include="Payloads\**" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
```

Reading from a file rather than inlining the JSON into the test is what keeps the sample regenerable without ever rewriting a test file — the test file stays entirely human-owned.

Sample value rules (deterministic, required members only — which also exercises the "optional absent" path):

| | value |
|---|---|
| `string` | `"sample-<jsonName>"` — unambiguously fake, greppable |
| `format: date-time` | `"2026-01-15T09:30:00+00:00"` — the literal already in the template |
| `format: date` | `"2026-01-15"` |
| `format: uuid` | `"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"` |
| `enum` | the first value in schema order |
| `const` | the const value |
| `integer` | `1`; `number` → `1.0`; `boolean` → `true` |
| `array` | exactly one element, recursed |
| object / `$ref` | recursed |
| `pattern` present, no `enum` | **omitted** — a generated string will not match an arbitrary regex, and inventing one that does is the forbidden guess |
| a gap member | omitted |

If an omission leaves a **required** member absent, the sample is not schema-valid, `Sample` reports `ok=false` with the reason, no file is written, and the template keeps its own literal with its honest comment. The `{{ if .contractGenerated }}` branch therefore needs a second condition — a separate `contractSampleGenerated` value, or the same key extended — so the test never reads a file that was not written. Simplest: make the sample a precondition of `contractGenerated` being set at all, and note that a schema whose required members are pattern-constrained gets no generation *and* no shell suppression. That keeps one flag and one invariant.

This is the last unit in the sequence precisely so it can be dropped without invalidating anything before it. Even if it is dropped, the one-line honest-comment change in the template should still ship.

## Specific risks

1. **Nested-record references in a primary constructor parameter list.** The generator emits fully qualified `<Root>.<Def>` to avoid depending on C# name lookup inside a type's own parameter list. If even the qualified form has an issue with a nested type of a `record` under construction, the fallback is top-level types with a per-schema `Contracts.<RootName>` sub-namespace — which reintroduces the collision problem the nesting solves. **Must be proven by `dotnet build` in step 3's live check, before step 8 commits the template change.** Highest risk in the plan.
2. **STJ constructor-parameter binding with `[property: JsonPropertyName]`.** The design leans on STJ matching a positional record's constructor parameters to their generated properties and honoring the property's `JsonPropertyName` for the wire name. Documented behavior, but it is the difference between a record that deserializes and one that silently produces nulls. Pin it in the scaffolded integration test, not only by inspection.
3. **Optional-parameter default semantics.** The `T? = null` choice makes STJ's handling of C# default parameter values irrelevant. If anyone "improves" this to a non-nullable default (`long Count = 0`), a missing property silently becomes `0`. The reason belongs in a "deliberately not" comment on the emitter, the pattern AGENTS.md points at `internal/gitops/remote.go` for.
4. **Positional-record order is source-breaking on schema evolution.** A new required property inserted mid-document shifts positional arguments in every hand-written call site. Unavoidable with positional records; mitigated by the header comment and by the fact that `with` expressions and serialization are unaffected. Worth noting in the shared-contracts `AGENTS.md.tmpl` too, since a migration agent reads that.
5. **`*.cs.tmpl` is a broad glob.** Any future non-sample `.cs.tmpl` added to the shared-contracts skeleton would be silently suppressed in generated mode. Mitigation: a comment on the rule, and a template-repo test that renders both modes and asserts the file set.
6. **The `obj/` tree committed into `shared-contracts/skeleton/`** ships build artifacts — including a `GlobalUsings.g.cs` — into every scaffolded project. Unrelated to this work, harmless to the `*.cs.tmpl` glob, and worth a separate cleanup commit. Flagging it because it makes "which `.g.cs` files are ours" ambiguous in exactly the tree this feature writes into.
7. **`decimal` for `number`** cannot represent every JSON double and throws on overflow. Chosen to match the existing sample and money semantics; `format: double` is the escape hatch. A registry schema carrying a scientific-notation float in a plain `number` would fail at deserialization. Note it in `Result.Notes` when a `number` has no `format`.
8. **`--force` deleting a scaffolded shell** is the only place in this design where the CLI removes a `.cs` file. Guarded by a bytes-match against the baseline shell render, but it is the operation most worth a second reviewer.
9. **Extractor asymmetry.** Only the loader has a `x-intropy-message-ref` parameter today, so only subscribers get generation. An extractor *publishing* a registry message would want the same records from the same schema, and that needs a publication-side message-ref parameter. Out of scope; the generator and orchestration are already template-agnostic, so it is additive. Say so, or someone will read the loader-only wiring as a design limit.
10. **Registry availability at create time.** Generation happens only inside the branch that already fetched the export, and `prepareCreateTemplate` already degrades a fetch failure to a warning. So a registry-down create still scaffolds — with a hand-written shell and `contractGenerated: false`. `int update` then fills it in later. Verify this path explicitly; it is the one that quietly changes the shape of the scaffolded project.
